snapshot.stmt: For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) and \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(\tau=\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}\) is identified, and under independent sample sizes \(n_E,n_O\) its canonical gradient decomposes into the two sample components \(\phi_{E,d}/n_E\) and \(\phi_{O,d}/n_O\), giving local variance \(V_{E,d}/n_E+V_{O,d}/n_O\).

defs.def:regular-law-class: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}=\{P: \text{long- and short-term consistency, observational latent exchangeability and overlap, experimental randomization and overlap, designwise middle-role external validity and source support hold, and the sequential restriction, both completeness conditions, selection-bridge existence, operator bijectivity, and nondegenerate score variances hold for every }d\in\mathcal D\text{ and }a\in\{0,1\}\}\).

assumptions.ass:early-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{1d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:late-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{3d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-outcomes: \((Y(a),S_{3d}(a))\perp S_{1d}(a)\mid S_{2d}(a),U,X,G=O\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).

snapshot.stmt: For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and fixed \(0<\alpha<1\), as \(B\to\infty\) the floor-count local semiparametric efficiency bound satisfies \(B\{V_{E,d}/n_{E,B}(d,\alpha)+V_{O,d}/n_{O,B}(d,\alpha)\}=\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)+\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)\), where \(0\le\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)\le 2B^{-1}\{V_{E,d}c_{E,d}^2/\alpha^2+V_{O,d}c_{O,d}^2/(1-\alpha)^2\}\) once \(B\ge2\max\{c_{E,d}/\alpha,c_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\}\). Hence the floor-count bound converges to \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\). The unique minimizer and minimum of this limiting profile are \(\alpha_d^*(P)=\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}/(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})\) and \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2\).

defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).

snapshot.stmt: For the full-catalogue pilot selector, \(0\le\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)-\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\le2\varepsilon_m\) deterministically, and \(\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\subseteq\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\). Thus \(P\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\le P\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\to0\), with the right-hand event empty when every design is optimal. Under \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\), and \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), \(\varepsilon_m=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat\alpha_{d,m}-\alpha_d^*(P)|=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m)\), and uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(B\{V_{E,d}/\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor+V_{O,d}/\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m+B^{-1})=o_P(1)\). The deterministic tie rule selects one empirical minimizer, while consistency means membership in the full population optimizer set \(D^*(P)\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.

snapshot.stmt: Let \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose that for fixed \(L\), uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(1\le\ell\le L\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{w,h,d}=O_P(\delta_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{2,O,h,d}=O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{w,q,d}=O_P(\delta_{q,B})\), and \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{2,O,q,d}=O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), where all four deterministic rates are \(o(1)\) and \(\min\{\delta_{h,B}\rho_{q,B},\rho_{h,B}\delta_{q,B}\}=o(B^{-1/2})\). Under the full-catalogue pilot law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\) with \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\) with \(r_{\widetilde V,B}=o(1)\). For \(\widehat d_m\) and the feasible share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), form the realized counts \(N_{E,B},N_{O,B}\) and define \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) from the selected foldwise source-score second moments. Then \(B\{V_{E,\widehat d_m}/N_{E,B}+V_{O,\widehat d_m}/N_{O,B}\}-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), \(\widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), \(\sqrt B(\widehat\tau_B-\tau)/\widehat s_B\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\), and the Wald interval has coverage tending to \(1-\eta\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.

Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).

defs.def:selected-wald-variance: For the selected design \(\widehat d_m\) and feasible pilot share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), use the realized counts \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\). For each main-study observation, evaluate its experimental or observational score using \(\widehat h_{\widehat d_m,B}^{(-\ell)}\) and \(\widehat q_{\widehat d_m,B}^{(-\ell)}\) trained outside its fold. Let \(\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}\) and \(\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}\) be the corresponding within-source empirical second moments, and set \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) and \(\widehat s_B=(\widehat s_B^2)^{1/2}\).

snapshot.stmt: If \(\mathcal D=\{d\}\), the main study fixes counts \(n_E,n_O\), and \(B=c_{E,d}n_E+c_{O,d}n_O\), then \(\mathcal V_d(c_{E,d}n_E/B;P)/B=V_{E,d}/n_E+V_{O,d}/n_O\), which is the Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang fixed-system efficiency bound.

For the explicit two-design family \(P_{\epsilon}\), every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives a law in \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\): both binary conditional-expectation matrices have nonzero determinant, both completeness conditions hold, and the displayed bridges satisfy \(\|h_d\|_{\infty}<\infty\), \(\|q_d\|_{\infty}<\infty\), and finite fourth moments for each \(d\). The two designs have equal costs \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=3\) and \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=4\), hence equal jointly budget-feasible sample sizes \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm p})=n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm e})=B/7\). Therefore the cost-aware comparator reduces within this equal-cost subclass to the displayed residual-variance ordering: \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}(P_{\epsilon};B)=7(1-\epsilon^2)(7/16)/[B(1-9\epsilon^2/16)]<21/(5B)=\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm e}}(P_{\epsilon};B)\). Thus \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\epsilon})=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), and the prespecified tie rule is immaterial on the witness path. Yet \(V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=4(1/16)(7/9)/[(15/16)^2\epsilon^2]+O(\epsilon^{-1})\), while \(V_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}\), \(V_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}\), and \(V_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}\) remain bounded and nondegenerate; consequently \(D^*(P_{\epsilon})=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\epsilon})\to\infty\). Moreover, every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\cap D^*(P)=\varnothing\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). Thus the cost-aware prediction-efficiency workflow of CarneiroLeeWilhelm2020 has no finite approximation-ratio analogue in this persistent-confounding bridge model.

defs.def:binary-region: Let \(\|P-P_{\epsilon}\|_{\mathrm{cell}}\) be the maximum absolute difference over the finitely many observable and latent cell probabilities in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\), and set \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}=\bigcup_{0<\epsilon<10^{-3}}\{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}:\|P-P_{\epsilon}\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<10^{-6}\epsilon^4\}\).
defs.def:binary-witness: Fix \(K=4\), \(c_j=1\) for every catalogue variable, \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), \(\kappa=2\), and let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form \(Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)})\), while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{3/4}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three; a prespecified deterministic order favors \(d_{\mathrm p}\) only if the cost-aware objectives tie. Both designs measure two catalogue variables, so \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=3\), \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=4\), and \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm p})=n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm e})=B/7\). For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the displayed bridges are \(h_d(l,a)=l/y\) and \(q_d(e,a)=\{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)\}/(1-1/16)\), the residual prediction variance is \(R(x,y)=(1-x^2)(1-y^2)/(1-x^2y^2)\), and equal joint costs imply \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=7R(x,y)/B\).
defs.def:regular-law-class: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}=\{P: \text{long- and short-term consistency, observational latent exchangeability and overlap, experimental randomization and overlap, designwise middle-role external validity and source support hold, and the sequential restriction, both completeness conditions, selection-bridge existence, operator bijectivity, and nondegenerate score variances hold for every }d\in\mathcal D\text{ and }a\in\{0,1\}\}\).
defs.def:predictive-benchmark: Compute \(R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O]\), charge the jointly budget-feasible paired-sample cost through \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=B/(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})\), and minimize the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped objective \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=R_d(P)/n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)/B\) over \(d\in\mathcal D\). Retain all objective minimizers in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\), use a prespecified deterministic order only to implement a tie, and evaluate \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)/\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\).

Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), no additional operator comparison is needed for a law-specific finite predictive guarantee:
\[
 1\le\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d'}V_{E,d'}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d'}V_{O,d'}})^2}<\infty.
\]
The smallest constant in the actual best-tie inequality is exactly \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\).  The least constant that makes every pairwise implication
\(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)\Rightarrow
\mathcal V_d^*(P)\le C(P)\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\)
valid is
\[
 \max_{\substack{d,d'\in\mathcal D:\,
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)}}
 \frac{\mathcal V_d^*(P)}{\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
There is no finite constant uniform over \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\).  Moreover, the sharp finite-catalogue constant is not in general the largest generalized eigenvalue of a transported quadratic-form pair; such an eigenvalue is sharp only under an additional richness and attainment condition for the catalogue directions, and two-sided quadratic-form comparison generally yields a generalized condition number rather than the largest eigenvalue alone.

snapshot.stmt: For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and fixed \(0<\alpha<1\), as \(B\to\infty\) the floor-count local semiparametric efficiency bound satisfies \(B\{V_{E,d}/n_{E,B}(d,\alpha)+V_{O,d}/n_{O,B}(d,\alpha)\}=\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)+\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)\), where \(0\le\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)\le 2B^{-1}\{V_{E,d}c_{E,d}^2/\alpha^2+V_{O,d}c_{O,d}^2/(1-\alpha)^2\}\) once \(B\ge2\max\{c_{E,d}/\alpha,c_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\}\). Hence the floor-count bound converges to \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\). The unique minimizer and minimum of this limiting profile are \(\alpha_d^*(P)=\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}/(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})\) and \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2\).

defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).

snapshot.stmt: For the full-catalogue pilot selector, \(0\le\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)-\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\le2\varepsilon_m\) deterministically, and \(\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\subseteq\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\). Thus \(P\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\le P\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\to0\), with the right-hand event empty when every design is optimal. Under \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\), and \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), \(\varepsilon_m=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat\alpha_{d,m}-\alpha_d^*(P)|=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m)\), and uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(B\{V_{E,d}/\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor+V_{O,d}/\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m+B^{-1})=o_P(1)\). The deterministic tie rule selects one empirical minimizer, while consistency means membership in the full population optimizer set \(D^*(P)\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.

snapshot.stmt: Let \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose that for fixed \(L\), uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(1\le\ell\le L\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{w,h,d}=O_P(\delta_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{2,O,h,d}=O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{w,q,d}=O_P(\delta_{q,B})\), and \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{2,O,q,d}=O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), where all four deterministic rates are \(o(1)\) and \(\min\{\delta_{h,B}\rho_{q,B},\rho_{h,B}\delta_{q,B}\}=o(B^{-1/2})\). Under the full-catalogue pilot law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\) with \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\) with \(r_{\widetilde V,B}=o(1)\). For \(\widehat d_m\) and the feasible share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), form the realized counts \(N_{E,B},N_{O,B}\) and define \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) from the selected foldwise source-score second moments. Then \(B\{V_{E,\widehat d_m}/N_{E,B}+V_{O,\widehat d_m}/N_{O,B}\}-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), \(\widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), \(\sqrt B(\widehat\tau_B-\tau)/\widehat s_B\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\), and the Wald interval has coverage tending to \(1-\eta\).

Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.
defs.def:selected-wald-variance: For the selected design \(\widehat d_m\) and feasible pilot share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), use the realized counts \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\). For each main-study observation, evaluate its experimental or observational score using \(\widehat h_{\widehat d_m,B}^{(-\ell)}\) and \(\widehat q_{\widehat d_m,B}^{(-\ell)}\) trained outside its fold. Let \(\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}\) and \(\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}\) be the corresponding within-source empirical second moments, and set \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) and \(\widehat s_B=(\widehat s_B^2)^{1/2}\).

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), no additional operator comparison is needed for a law-specific finite predictive guarantee:
\[
 1\le\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d'}V_{E,d'}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d'}V_{O,d'}})^2}<\infty.
\]
The smallest constant in the actual best-tie inequality is exactly \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\).  The least constant that makes every pairwise implication
\(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)\Rightarrow
\mathcal V_d^*(P)\le C(P)\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\)
valid is
\[
 \max_{\substack{d,d'\in\mathcal D:\,
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)}}
 \frac{\mathcal V_d^*(P)}{\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
There is no finite constant uniform over \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\).  Moreover, the sharp finite-catalogue constant is not in general the largest generalized eigenvalue of a transported quadratic-form pair; such an eigenvalue is sharp only under an additional richness and attainment condition for the catalogue directions, and two-sided quadratic-form comparison generally yields a generalized condition number rather than the largest eigenvalue alone.

defs.def:operator-comparison-handle: Use \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{comp}}\) to compare generalized eigenvalues of the source-gradient quadratic forms after transporting the cost-weighted predictive residual directions in \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\) through \(T_d^{-1}\), with the target object being a law-primitive constant that upper-bounds \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\) without directly assuming a design-value inequality.
defs.def:predictive-benchmark: Compute \(R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O]\), charge the jointly budget-feasible paired-sample cost through \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=B/(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})\), and minimize the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped objective \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=R_d(P)/n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)/B\) over \(d\in\mathcal D\). Retain all objective minimizers in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\), use a prespecified deterministic order only to implement a tie, and evaluate \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)/\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\).
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

Under \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\), and \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), \(\varepsilon_m=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat\alpha_{d,m}-\alpha_d^*(P)|=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m)\), and uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(B\{V_{E,d}/\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor+V_{O,d}/\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m+B^{-1})=o_P(1)\). The deterministic tie rule selects one empirical minimizer, while consistency means membership in the full population optimizer set \(D^*(P)\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.

snapshot.stmt: Let \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose that for fixed \(L\), uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(1\le\ell\le L\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{w,h,d}=O_P(\delta_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{2,O,h,d}=O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{w,q,d}=O_P(\delta_{q,B})\), and \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{2,O,q,d}=O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), where all four deterministic rates are \(o(1)\) and \(\min\{\delta_{h,B}\rho_{q,B},\rho_{h,B}\delta_{q,B}\}=o(B^{-1/2})\). Under the full-catalogue pilot law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\) with \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\) with \(r_{\widetilde V,B}=o(1)\). For \(\widehat d_m\) and the feasible share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), form the realized counts \(N_{E,B},N_{O,B}\) and define \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) from the selected foldwise source-score second moments. Then \(B\{V_{E,\widehat d_m}/N_{E,B}+V_{O,\widehat d_m}/N_{O,B}\}-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), \(\widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), \(\sqrt B(\widehat\tau_B-\tau)/\widehat s_B\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\), and the Wald interval has coverage tending to \(1-\eta\).

defs.def:selected-wald-variance: For the selected design \(\widehat d_m\) and feasible pilot share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), use the realized counts \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\). snapshot.stmt: For the explicit two-design family \(P_{\epsilon}\), every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives a law in \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\): both binary conditional-expectation matrices have nonzero determinant, both completeness conditions hold, and the displayed bridges satisfy \(\|h_d\|_{\infty}<\infty\), \(\|q_d\|_{\infty}<\infty\), and finite fourth moments for each \(d\). The two designs have equal costs \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=3\) and \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=4\), hence equal jointly budget-feasible sample sizes \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm p})=n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm e})=B/7\). Therefore the cost-aware comparator reduces within this equal-cost subclass to the displayed residual-variance ordering: \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}(P_{\epsilon};B)=7(1-\epsilon^2)(7/16)/[B(1-9\epsilon^2/16)]<21/(5B)=\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm e}}(P_{\epsilon};B)\). Thus \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\epsilon})=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), and the prespecified tie rule is immaterial on the witness path. Yet \(V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=4(1/16)(7/9)/[(15/16)^2\epsilon^2]+O(\epsilon^{-1})\), while \(V_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}\), \(V_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}\), and \(V_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}\) remain bounded and nondegenerate; consequently \(D^*(P_{\epsilon})=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\epsilon})\to\infty\). Moreover, every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\cap D^*(P)=\varnothing\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). Thus the cost-aware prediction-efficiency workflow of CarneiroLeeWilhelm2020 has no finite approximation-ratio analogue in this persistent-confounding bridge model.

defs.def:binary-region: Restrict \(P\) to the same finite binary support for \((G,U,T,W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)},Y(0),Y(1))\) as in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\), let \(\|P-P_{\epsilon}\|_{\mathrm{cell}}\) be the maximum absolute difference over the complete joint latent-cell probability vector on that fixed support, and set \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}=\bigcup_{0<\epsilon<10^{-3}}\{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}:\|P-P_{\epsilon}\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<10^{-6}\epsilon^4\}\).
defs.def:binary-witness: Fix \(K=4\), \(c_j=1\) for every catalogue variable, \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), \(\kappa=2\), and let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form \(Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)})\), while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{3/4}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three; a prespecified deterministic order favors \(d_{\mathrm p}\) only if the cost-aware objectives tie. Both designs measure two catalogue variables, so \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=3\), \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=4\), and \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm p})=n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm e})=B/7\). For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the displayed bridges are \(h_d(l,a)=l/y\) and \(q_d(e,a)=\{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)\}/(1-1/16)\), the residual prediction variance is \(R(x,y)=(1-x^2)(1-y^2)/(1-x^2y^2)\), and equal joint costs imply \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=7R(x,y)/B\).
defs.def:regular-law-class: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}=\{P: \text{long- and short-term consistency, observational latent exchangeability and overlap, experimental randomization and overlap, designwise full-short-term external validity and source support hold, and the sequential restriction, both completeness conditions, selection-bridge existence, operator bijectivity, and nondegenerate score variances hold for every }d\in\mathcal D\text{ and }a\in\{0,1\}\}\).
defs.def:predictive-benchmark: Compute \(R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O]\), charge the jointly budget-feasible paired-sample cost through \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=B/(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})\), and minimize the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped objective \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=R_d(P)/n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)/B\) over \(d\in\mathcal D\). Retain all objective minimizers in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\), use a prespecified deterministic order only to implement a tie, and evaluate \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)/\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\).
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).

For the unequal-cost binary construction, every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives \(P_{\epsilon}\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), the predictive optimizer is \(d_{\mathrm p}\), and the design-value optimizer is \(d_{\mathrm e}\).  Moreover,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{448}{2025\epsilon^2}+\frac{6272}{2025},\qquad

 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\epsilon})=\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]

snapshot.stmt:
For the unequal-cost binary witness, every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives a law \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) for which both designs identify \(\tau\) and are regular.  Although \(d_{\mathrm p}\) is more expensive, with \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=6>5=c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}\), it is the unique minimizer of this paper's Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped paired-source prediction objective, while \(d_{\mathrm e}\) is the unique minimizer of the causal design value.  More precisely,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{448}{2025\epsilon^2}+\frac{6272}{2025},qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)=\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\).  The same divergence holds on the relatively open range of cap-feasible cost vectors satisfying
\[
 1<\frac{c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}}
 {c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}}<\frac{48}{35},
\]
for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\).  Thus the failure is neither an equal-cost artifact nor an identification failure.

defs.def:binary-region: Restrict \(P\) to the same finite binary support for \((G,U,T,W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)},Y(0),Y(1))\) as in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\), let \(\|P-P_{\epsilon}\|_{\mathrm{cell}}\) be the maximum absolute difference over the complete joint latent-cell probability vector on that fixed support, and set \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}=\bigcup_{0<\epsilon<10^{-3}}\{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}:\|P-P_{\epsilon}\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<10^{-6}\epsilon^4\}\).
defs.def:binary-witness: Fix \(K=4\), \(c_j=1\) for every catalogue variable, \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), \(\kappa=2\), and let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form \(Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)})\), while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{3/4}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three; a prespecified deterministic order favors \(d_{\mathrm p}\) only if the cost-aware objectives tie. Both designs measure two catalogue variables, so \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=3\), \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=4\), and \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm p})=n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm e})=B/7\). For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the displayed bridges are \(h_d(l,a)=l/y\) and \(q_d(e,a)=\{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)\}/(1-1/16)\), the residual prediction variance is \(R(x,y)=(1-x^2)(1-y^2)/(1-x^2y^2)\), and equal joint costs imply \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=7R(x,y)/B\).
defs.def:regular-law-class: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}=\{P: \text{long- and short-term consistency, observational latent exchangeability and overlap, experimental randomization and overlap, designwise full-short-term external validity and source support hold, and the sequential restriction, both completeness conditions, selection-bridge existence, operator bijectivity, and nondegenerate score variances hold for every }d\in\mathcal D\text{ and }a\in\{0,1\}\}\).
defs.def:predictive-benchmark: Compute \(R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O]\), charge the jointly budget-feasible paired-sample cost through \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=B/(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})\), and minimize the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped objective \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=R_d(P)/n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)/B\) over \(d\in\mathcal D\). Retain all objective minimizers in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\), use a prespecified deterministic order only to implement a tie, and evaluate \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)/\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\).
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-outcomes: \((Y(a),S_{3d}(a))\perp S_{1d}(a)\mid S_{2d}(a),U,X,G=O\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:late-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{3d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:early-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{1d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

snapshot.stmt: For the full-catalogue pilot selector, \(0\le\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)-\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\le2\varepsilon_m\) deterministically, and \(\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\subseteq\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\). Thus \(P\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\le P\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\to0\), with the right-hand event empty when every design is optimal. Under \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\), and \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), \(\varepsilon_m=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat\alpha_{d,m}-\alpha_d^*(P)|=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m)\), and uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(B\{V_{E,d}/\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor+V_{O,d}/\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m+B^{-1})=o_P(1)\). The deterministic tie rule selects one empirical minimizer, while consistency means membership in the full population optimizer set \(D^*(P)\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.

snapshot.stmt: Let \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose that for fixed \(L\), uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(1\le\ell\le L\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{w,h,d}=O_P(\delta_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{2,O,h,d}=O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{w,q,d}=O_P(\delta_{q,B})\), and \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{2,O,q,d}=O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), where all four deterministic rates are \(o(1)\) and \(\min\{\delta_{h,B}\rho_{q,B},\rho_{h,B}\delta_{q,B}\}=o(B^{-1/2})\). Under the full-catalogue pilot law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\) with \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\) with \(r_{\widetilde V,B}=o(1)\). For \(\widehat d_m\) and the feasible share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), form the realized counts \(N_{E,B},N_{O,B}\) and define \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) from the selected foldwise source-score second moments. Then \(B\{V_{E,\widehat d_m}/N_{E,B}+V_{O,\widehat d_m}/N_{O,B}\}-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), \(\widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), \(\sqrt B(\widehat\tau_B-\tau)/\widehat s_B\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\), and the Wald interval has coverage tending to \(1-\eta\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.
defs.def:selected-wald-variance: For the selected design \(\widehat d_m\) and feasible pilot share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), use the realized counts \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\). For each main-study observation, evaluate its experimental or observational score using \(\widehat h_{\widehat d_m,B}^{(-\ell)}\) and \(\widehat q_{\widehat d_m,B}^{(-\ell)}\) trained outside its fold. Let \(\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}\) and \(\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}\) be the corresponding within-source empirical second moments, and set \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) and \(\widehat s_B=(\widehat s_B^2)^{1/2}\).

assumptions.ass:independent-pilot: \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main-study observations used to construct \(\widehat\tau_B\).
assumptions.ass:main-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.
assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.
assumptions.ass:uniform-outcome-strong-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{2,O,h,d}=O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.
assumptions.ass:uniform-outcome-weak-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{w,h,d}=O_P(\delta_{h,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.
assumptions.ass:uniform-selection-strong-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{2,O,q,d}=O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.
assumptions.ass:uniform-selection-weak-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{w,q,d}=O_P(\delta_{q,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.

snapshot.stmt: For the explicit two-design family \(P_{\epsilon}\), every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives a law in \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\): both binary conditional-expectation matrices have nonzero determinant, both completeness conditions hold, and the displayed bridges satisfy \(\|h_d\|_{\infty}<\infty\), \(\|q_d\|_{\infty}<\infty\), and finite fourth moments for each \(d\). The two designs have equal costs \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=3\) and \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=4\), hence equal jointly budget-feasible sample sizes \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm p})=n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm e})=B/7\). Therefore the cost-aware comparator reduces within this equal-cost subclass to the displayed residual-variance ordering: \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}(P_{\epsilon};B)=7(1-\epsilon^2)(7/16)/[B(1-9\epsilon^2/16)]<21/(5B)=\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm e}}(P_{\epsilon};B)\). Thus \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\epsilon})=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), and the prespecified tie rule is immaterial on the witness path. Yet \(V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=4(1/16)(7/9)/[(15/16)^2\epsilon^2]+O(\epsilon^{-1})\), while \(V_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}\), \(V_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}\), and \(V_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}\) remain bounded and nondegenerate; consequently \(D^*(P_{\epsilon})=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\epsilon})\to\infty\). Moreover, every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\cap D^*(P)=\varnothing\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). Thus the cost-aware prediction-efficiency workflow of CarneiroLeeWilhelm2020 has no finite approximation-ratio analogue in this persistent-confounding bridge model.

defs.def:binary-witness: Fix \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=3/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=2\), and let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form \(Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)})\), while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{3/4}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=5/2\), \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=7/2\), \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2\), and \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3\), so the prediction-selected design is genuinely more expensive and \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm p})=B/6<n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm e})=B/5\). For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are \(h_d(l,a)=l/y\) and \(q_d(e,a)=\{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)\}/(1-1/16)\), and the residual prediction variance is \(R(x,y)=(1-x^2)(1-y^2)/(1-x^2y^2)\).

Retain all objective minimizers in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\), use a prespecified deterministic order only to implement a tie, and evaluate \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)/\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\).

Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).

assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-outcomes: \((Y(a),S_{3d}(a))\perp S_{1d}(a)\mid S_{2d}(a),U,X,G=O\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), no additional operator comparison is needed for a law-specific finite predictive guarantee:
\[
 1\le\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d'}V_{E,d'}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d'}V_{O,d'}})^2}<\infty.
\]
The smallest constant in the actual best-tie inequality is exactly \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\).  The least constant that makes every pairwise implication
\(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)\Rightarrow
\mathcal V_d^*(P)\le C(P)\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\)
valid is
\[
 \max_{\substack{d,d'\in\mathcal D:\,
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)}}
 \frac{\mathcal V_d^*(P)}{\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
There is no finite constant uniform over \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\).  Moreover, the sharp finite-catalogue constant is not in general the largest generalized eigenvalue of a transported quadratic-form pair; such an eigenvalue is sharp only under an additional richness and attainment condition for the catalogue directions, and two-sided quadratic-form comparison generally yields a generalized condition number rather than the largest eigenvalue alone.

defs.def:operator-comparison-handle: Use \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{comp}}\) to compare generalized eigenvalues of the source-gradient quadratic forms after transporting the cost-weighted predictive residual directions in \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\) through \(T_d^{-1}\), with the target object being a law-primitive constant that upper-bounds \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\) without directly assuming a design-value inequality.

For the unequal-cost binary construction, every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives \(P_{\epsilon}\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), the predictive optimizer is \(d_{\mathrm p}\), and the design-value optimizer is \(d_{\mathrm e}\).  Moreover,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{448}{2025\epsilon^2}+\frac{6272}{2025},\qquad
 \mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e}}^*(P_{\epsilon})=\frac{3872}{25},\qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\epsilon})=\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
For each fixed \(\epsilon\) there is a radius \(r_\epsilon>0\) such that every law in the constrained fixed-support regular model within cell distance \(r_\epsilon\) of \(P_\epsilon\) has the same two strict optimizer assignments and has \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)>\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)/2\).

For the unequal-cost binary witness, every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives a law \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) for which both designs identify \(\tau\) and are regular. More precisely,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{448}{2025\epsilon^2}+\frac{6272}{2025},qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)=\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\).  The same divergence holds on the relatively open range of cap-feasible cost vectors satisfying
\[
 1<\frac{c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}}
 {c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}}<\frac{48}{35},
\]
for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\).  Thus the failure is neither an equal-cost artifact nor an identification failure.

Thus \(P\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\le P\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\to0\), with the right-hand event empty when every design is optimal. snapshot.stmt:
Let \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\), and assume that \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main-study observations used to construct \(\widehat\tau_B\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose that for fixed \(L\), uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(1\le\ell\le L\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{w,h,d}=O_P(\delta_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{2,O,h,d}=O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{w,q,d}=O_P(\delta_{q,B})\), and \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{2,O,q,d}=O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), where all four deterministic rates are \(o(1)\) and \(\min\{\delta_{h,B}\rho_{q,B},\rho_{h,B}\delta_{q,B}\}=o(B^{-1/2})\). Under the full-catalogue pilot law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\) with \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\) with \(r_{\widetilde V,B}=o(1)\). For \(\widehat d_m\) and the feasible share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), form the realized counts \(N_{E,B},N_{O,B}\) and define \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) from the selected foldwise source-score second moments. Then \(B\{V_{E,\widehat d_m}/N_{E,B}+V_{O,\widehat d_m}/N_{O,B}\}-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), \(\widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), and
\[
 \frac{\sqrt B\{\widehat\tau_B-(\mu_{\widehat d_m,1}-\mu_{\widehat d_m,0})\}}
 {\widehat s_B}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
The corresponding two-sided standard-normal Wald interval has coverage tending to \(1-\eta\) for the pilot-selected bridge contrast \(\mu_{\widehat d_m,1}-\mu_{\widehat d_m,0}\). If, in addition, \(\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}=\tau\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\), then the same studentized limit is centered at \(\tau\) and the same interval has coverage tending to \(1-\eta\) for the observational-population long-term average treatment effect.

defs.def:selected-wald-variance: For the selected design \(\widehat d_m\) and feasible pilot share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), use the realized counts \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\). snapshot.stmt:
For the unequal-cost binary witness, every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives a law \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) for which both designs identify \(\tau\) and are regular. Although \(d_{\mathrm p}\) is more expensive, with \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=6>5=c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}\), it is the unique minimizer of this paper's Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped paired-source prediction objective, while \(d_{\mathrm e}\) is the unique minimizer of the causal design value. More precisely,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{448}{2025\epsilon^2}+\frac{6272}{2025},\qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)=\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). The same divergence holds on the relatively open range of cap-feasible cost vectors satisfying
\[
 1<\frac{c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}}
 {c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}}<\frac{48}{35},
\]
for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\). Thus the failure is neither an equal-cost artifact nor an identification failure.

defs.def:binary-witness: Fix \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=3/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=2\), and let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form \(Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)})\), while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{3/4}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=5/2\), \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=7/2\), \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2\), and \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3\), so the prediction-selected design is genuinely more expensive and \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm p})=B/6<n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm e})=B/5\). Retain all objective minimizers in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\), use a prespecified deterministic order only to implement a tie, and evaluate \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)/\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\).

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), the exact fixed-catalogue diagnostic identity is
\[
 1\le\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d'}V_{E,d'}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d'}V_{O,d'}})^2}<\infty.
\]
The smallest constant in the actual best-tie inequality is exactly \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\). The least constant that makes every pairwise implication
\(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)\Rightarrow \mathcal V_d^*(P)\le C(P)\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\)
valid is
\[
 \max_{\substack{d,d'\in\mathcal D:\,
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)}}
 \frac{\mathcal V_d^*(P)}{\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
Every displayed constant is finite at a fixed \(P\), but \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). Thus finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) yields an exact law-specific enumeration, not a primitive uniform predictive-efficiency guarantee.

\[

Under \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\), and \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), \(\varepsilon_m=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat\alpha_{d,m}-\alpha_d^*(P)|=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m)\), and uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(B\{V_{E,d}/\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor+V_{O,d}/\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m+B^{-1})=o_P(1)\). \[

 \le
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{c_{E,d},c_{O,d},V_{E,d},V_{O,d}\}<\infty.
\]
Suppose
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\bigl\{
 |\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,
 |\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\bigr\}=O_P(r_{V,m}),
 \qquad r_{V,m}=o(1),
 \qquad \underline v_m\downarrow0,
\]
and define \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}\) by the full-catalogue pilot selector.  Then, along every joint sequence \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\),
\[

 \frac{V_{E,d}}{\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor}
 +\frac{V_{O,d}}{\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor}
 \right\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)\right|
 =O_P\!\left((r_{V,m}+\underline v_m)^2+B^{-1}\right).
\]

snapshot.stmt: If \(\mathcal D=\{d\}\), the main study fixes counts \(n_E,n_O\), and \(B=c_{E,d}n_E+c_{O,d}n_O\), then \(\mathcal V_d(c_{E,d}n_E/B;P)/B=V_{E,d}/n_E+V_{O,d}/n_O\), which is the Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang fixed-system efficiency bound.

For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), the exact fixed-catalogue diagnostic identity is
\[
 1\le\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d'}V_{E,d'}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d'}V_{O,d'}})^2}<\infty.
\]
The smallest constant in the actual best-tie inequality is exactly \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\). The least constant that makes every pairwise implication
\(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)\Rightarrow \mathcal V_d^*(P)\le C(P)\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\)
valid is
\[
 \max_{\substack{d,d'\in\mathcal D:\,
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)}}
 \frac{\mathcal V_d^*(P)}{\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
Every displayed constant is finite at a fixed \(P\), but \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). Thus finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) yields an exact law-specific enumeration, not a primitive uniform predictive-efficiency guarantee.

defs.def:predictive-benchmark: Compute \(R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O]\), charge the jointly budget-feasible paired-sample cost through \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=B/(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})\), and minimize the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped objective \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=R_d(P)/n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)/B\) over \(d\in\mathcal D\). Retain all objective minimizers in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\), use a prespecified deterministic order only to implement a tie, and evaluate \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)/\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\).

defs.def:regular-law-class: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}=\{P: \text{long- and short-term consistency, observational latent exchangeability and overlap, experimental randomization and overlap, designwise full-short-term external validity and source support hold, and the sequential restriction, both completeness conditions, selection-bridge existence, operator bijectivity, and nondegenerate score variances hold for every }d\in\mathcal D\text{ and }a\in\{0,1\}\}\).

assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).

assumptions.ass:late-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{3d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:early-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{1d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.

snapshot.stmt:
For the unequal-cost binary construction, every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives \(P_{\epsilon}\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), the predictive optimizer is \(d_{\mathrm p}\), and the design-value optimizer is \(d_{\mathrm e}\).  Moreover,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{448}{2025\epsilon^2}+\frac{6272}{2025},\qquad
 \mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e}}^*(P_{\epsilon})=\frac{3872}{25},\qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\epsilon})=\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
For each fixed \(\epsilon\) there is a radius \(r_\epsilon>0\) such that every law in the constrained fixed-support regular model within cell distance \(r_\epsilon\) of \(P_\epsilon\) has the same two strict optimizer assignments and has \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)>\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)/2\).

defs.def:binary-witness: Fix \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=3/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=2\), and let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form \(Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)})\), while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{3/4}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=5/2\), \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=7/2\), \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2\), and \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3\), so the prediction-selected design is genuinely more expensive and \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm p})=B/6<n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm e})=B/5\). For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are \(h_d(l,a)=l/y\) and \(q_d(e,a)=\{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)\}/(1-1/16)\), and the residual prediction variance is \(R(x,y)=(1-x^2)(1-y^2)/(1-x^2y^2)\).
defs.def:regular-law-class: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}=\{P: \text{long- and short-term consistency, observational latent exchangeability and overlap, experimental randomization and overlap, designwise full-short-term external validity and source support hold, and the sequential restriction, both completeness conditions, selection-bridge existence, operator bijectivity, and nondegenerate score variances hold for every }d\in\mathcal D\text{ and }a\in\{0,1\}\}\).
defs.def:predictive-benchmark: Compute \(R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O]\), charge the jointly budget-feasible paired-sample cost through \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=B/(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})\), and minimize the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped objective \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=R_d(P)/n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)/B\) over \(d\in\mathcal D\). Retain all objective minimizers in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\), use a prespecified deterministic order only to implement a tie, and evaluate \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)/\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\).
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

snapshot.stmt: For the full-catalogue pilot selector, \(0\le\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)-\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\le2\varepsilon_m\) deterministically, and \(\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\subseteq\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\). Thus \(P\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\le P\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\to0\), with the right-hand event empty when every design is optimal. Under \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\), and \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), \(\varepsilon_m=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat\alpha_{d,m}-\alpha_d^*(P)|=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m)\), and uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(B\{V_{E,d}/\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor+V_{O,d}/\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m+B^{-1})=o_P(1)\). The deterministic tie rule selects one empirical minimizer, while consistency means membership in the full population optimizer set \(D^*(P)\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\), assume \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), and assume that \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main-study observations used to construct \(\widehat\tau_B\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose that for fixed \(L\), uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(1\le\ell\le L\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{w,h,d}=O_P(\delta_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{2,O,h,d}=O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{w,q,d}=O_P(\delta_{q,B})\), and \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{2,O,q,d}=O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), where all four deterministic rates are \(o(1)\) and \(\min\{\delta_{h,B}\rho_{q,B},\rho_{h,B}\delta_{q,B}\}=o(B^{-1/2})\). Under the full-catalogue pilot law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\) with \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\) with \(r_{\widetilde V,B}=o(1)\). For \(\widehat d_m\) and the feasible share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), form the realized counts \(N_{E,B},N_{O,B}\) and define \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) from the selected foldwise source-score second moments. Then \(B\{V_{E,\widehat d_m}/N_{E,B}+V_{O,\widehat d_m}/N_{O,B}\}-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), \(\widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), and
\[
 \frac{\sqrt B\{\widehat\tau_B-(\mu_{\widehat d_m,1}-\mu_{\widehat d_m,0})\}}
 {\widehat s_B}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
Let \(z_{1-\eta/2}\) be the \((1-\eta/2)\)-quantile of the standard normal law and define
\[
 I_B=\left[
 \widehat\tau_B-z_{1-\eta/2}\frac{\widehat s_B}{\sqrt B},
 \widehat\tau_B+z_{1-\eta/2}\frac{\widehat s_B}{\sqrt B}
 \right].
\]
Then \(P\{\mu_{\widehat d_m,1}-\mu_{\widehat d_m,0}\in I_B\}\to1-\eta\). If, in addition, \(\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}=\tau\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\), then the same studentized limit is centered at \(\tau\) and \(P\{\tau\in I_B\}\to1-\eta\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.
defs.def:selected-wald-variance: For the selected design \(\widehat d_m\) and feasible pilot share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), use the realized counts \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\). For each main-study observation, evaluate its experimental or observational score using \(\widehat h_{\widehat d_m,B}^{(-\ell)}\) and \(\widehat q_{\widehat d_m,B}^{(-\ell)}\) trained outside its fold. Let \(\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}\) and \(\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}\) be the corresponding within-source empirical second moments, and set \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) and \(\widehat s_B=(\widehat s_B^2)^{1/2}\).

assumptions.ass:independent-pilot: \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main-study observations used to construct \(\widehat\tau_B\).
assumptions.ass:main-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.

assumptions.ass:uniform-selection-weak-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{w,q,d}=O_P(\delta_{q,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.

snapshot.stmt: If \(\mathcal D=\{d\}\), the main study fixes counts \(n_E,n_O\), and \(B=c_{E,d}n_E+c_{O,d}n_O\), then \(\mathcal V_d(c_{E,d}n_E/B;P)/B=V_{E,d}/n_E+V_{O,d}/n_O\), which is the Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang fixed-system efficiency bound.

For the unequal-cost binary witness, every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives a law \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) for which both designs identify \(\tau\) and are regular. Although \(d_{\mathrm p}\) is more expensive, with \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=6>5=c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}\), it is the unique minimizer of this paper's Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped paired-source prediction objective, while \(d_{\mathrm e}\) is the unique minimizer of the causal design value. More precisely,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{448}{2025\epsilon^2}+\frac{6272}{2025},\qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)=\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). The same divergence holds on the relatively open range of cap-feasible cost vectors satisfying
\[
 1<\frac{c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}}
 {c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}}<\frac{48}{35},
\]
for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\). Thus the failure is neither an equal-cost artifact nor an identification failure.
