snapshot.stmt:
For every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), consider the finite family of binary-support laws that retain the witness equalities \(A=(T+1)/2\), \(Z(a)=(W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4)\), \(Y(a)=U\), constant \(X,S_{2d}\), the two fixed role assignments, and the strictly positive factorization
\[
 P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
 =\pi_g\nu_u
 \bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t+\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}
 \prod_{j=1}^4 k_{j,u}(w_j).
\]
There is \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{reg}}>0\) such that every law \(P\) in this constrained family with \(\|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{reg}}\) belongs to \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\).  Hence the regular locus is a relative neighborhood of \(P_\epsilon\) in the constrained family; regularity is not imposed by intersecting the neighborhood with \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\).

defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). defs.def:predictive-benchmark: Compute \(R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O]\), charge the jointly budget-feasible paired-sample cost through \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=B/(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})\), and minimize the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped objective \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=R_d(P)/n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)/B\) over \(d\in\mathcal D\). Retain all objective minimizers in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\), use a prespecified deterministic order only to implement a tie, and evaluate \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)/\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\).
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

Let \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\), assume \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), and assume that \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main-study observations used to construct \(\widehat\tau_B\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose that for fixed \(L\), uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(1\le\ell\le L\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{w,h,d}=O_P(\delta_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{2,O,h,d}=O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{w,q,d}=O_P(\delta_{q,B})\), and \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{2,O,q,d}=O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), where all four deterministic rates are \(o(1)\) and \(\min\{\delta_{h,B}\rho_{q,B},\rho_{h,B}\delta_{q,B}\}=o(B^{-1/2})\). Under the full-catalogue pilot law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\) with \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\) with \(r_{\widetilde V,B}=o(1)\). For \(\widehat d_m\) and the feasible share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), form the realized counts \(N_{E,B},N_{O,B}\) and define \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) from the selected foldwise source-score second moments. Then \(B\{V_{E,\widehat d_m}/N_{E,B}+V_{O,\widehat d_m}/N_{O,B}\}-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), \(\widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), and
\[
 \frac{\sqrt B\{\widehat\tau_B-(\mu_{\widehat d_m,1}-\mu_{\widehat d_m,0})\}}
 {\widehat s_B}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
Let \(z_{1-\eta/2}\) be the \((1-\eta/2)\)-quantile of the standard normal law and define
\[
 I_B=\left[
 \widehat\tau_B-z_{1-\eta/2}\frac{\widehat s_B}{\sqrt B},
 \widehat\tau_B+z_{1-\eta/2}\frac{\widehat s_B}{\sqrt B}
 \right].
\]
Then \(P\{\mu_{\widehat d_m,1}-\mu_{\widehat d_m,0}\in I_B\}\to1-\eta\). If, in addition, \(\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}=\tau\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\), then the same studentized limit is centered at \(\tau\) and \(P\{\tau\in I_B\}\to1-\eta\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.
defs.def:selected-wald-variance: For the selected design \(\widehat d_m\) and feasible pilot share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), use the realized counts \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\). For each main-study observation, evaluate its experimental or observational score using \(\widehat h_{\widehat d_m,B}^{(-\ell)}\) and \(\widehat q_{\widehat d_m,B}^{(-\ell)}\) trained outside its fold. Let \(\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}\) and \(\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}\) be the corresponding within-source empirical second moments, and set \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) and \(\widehat s_B=(\widehat s_B^2)^{1/2}\).

For the unequal-cost binary witness, every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives a law \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) for which both designs identify \(\tau\) and are regular. Although \(d_{\mathrm p}\) is more expensive, with \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=6>5=c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}\), it is the unique minimizer of this paper's Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped paired-source prediction objective, while \(d_{\mathrm e}\) is the unique minimizer of the causal design value. More precisely,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{448}{2025\epsilon^2}+\frac{6272}{2025},\qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)=\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). The same divergence holds on the relatively open range of cap-feasible cost vectors satisfying
\[
 1<\frac{c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}}
 {c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}}<\frac{48}{35},
\]
for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\). Thus the failure is neither an equal-cost artifact nor an identification failure.

defs.def:binary-region:
Fix the catalogue, costs, cap, and the two role assignments exactly as in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\).  Name as the \emph{binary constrained finite-cell model} the family \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}\) of laws \(P\) with constant \(X\) and constant \(S_{2d}\), latent variables \(U,T,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4\in\{-1,1\}\), \(A=(T+1)/2\), and potential variables
\[
 Z(a)=(W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4),\qquad Y(a)=U,qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For strictly positive probability vectors \((\pi_g:g\in\{E,O\})\), \((\nu_u:u\in\{-1,1\})\), \((\lambda_t:t\in\{-1,1\})\), observational treatment kernels \(e_u(t)\), and proxy kernels \(k_{j,u}(w)\), its latent-cell mass factorizes as
\[
 P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
 =\pi_g\nu_u
 \bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t+\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}
 \prod_{j=1}^4 k_{j,u}(w_j).                                    \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(U\) is independent of \(G\), treatment is randomized independently of \(U\) in source \(E\), and the four proxies are mutually independent conditional on \(U\) and invariant across source and treatment.  The design \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \((W_1,W_2)\) to roles one and three, and \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \((W_3,W_4)\) to roles one and three; role two is constant.  The witness \(P_\epsilon\) is the point having \(\pi_E=\pi_O=1/2\), \(\nu_{-1}=\nu_1=1/2\), \(\lambda_{-1}=\lambda_1=1/2\), \(e_u(t)=(1+tu/4)/2\), and
\[
 k_{j,u}(w)=\frac{1+s_juw}{2},
 \qquad (s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4)=(\epsilon,3/4,1/2,1/2).
\]
The model is parameterized by the relative interiors of these finite probability simplices.  Its relative topology is equivalently the Euclidean parameter topology or the maximum-norm topology induced by the complete latent-cell vector in (1).  For every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), let \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{reg}}>0\) be furnished by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}regular\text{-}locus\text{-}relatively\text{-}open}\), and let \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{opt}}>0\) be the optimizer-stability radius furnished by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}witness\text{-}stability}\).  Choose
\[
 0<\delta_\epsilon<\min\{r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{reg}},r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{opt}}\}
\]
and define
\[
 \mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}
 =\bigcup_{0<\epsilon<10^{-3}}
 \left\{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}:
 \|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<\delta_\epsilon\right\}.     \tag{2}
\]
Thus each set in the union is a relative open ball in the named model, and \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is relatively open there.  The regular-neighborhood lemma proves, rather than defines, that \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\).  No claim of openness in the ambient unrestricted probability simplex is made, because the factorization, support, consistency, and causal equality restrictions define a lower-dimensional model.
defs.def:binary-witness: Fix \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=3/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=2\), and let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form \(Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)})\), while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Then \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=5/2\), \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=7/2\), \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2\), and \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3\), so the prediction-selected design is genuinely more expensive and \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm p})=B/6<n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm e})=B/5\). For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), the exact fixed-catalogue diagnostic identity is
\[
 1\le\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d'}V_{E,d'}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d'}V_{O,d'}})^2}<\infty.
\]
The smallest constant in the actual best-tie inequality is exactly \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\). The least constant that makes every pairwise implication
\(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)\Rightarrow \mathcal V_d^*(P)\le C(P)\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\)
valid is
\[
 \max_{\substack{d,d'\in\mathcal D:\,
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)}}
 \frac{\mathcal V_d^*(P)}{\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
Every displayed constant is finite at a fixed \(P\), but \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). Thus finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) yields an exact law-specific enumeration, not a primitive uniform predictive-efficiency guarantee.

For the unequal-cost binary construction, every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives \(P_{\epsilon}\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), the predictive optimizer is \(d_{\mathrm p}\), and the design-value optimizer is \(d_{\mathrm e}\).  Moreover,

 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\epsilon})=\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
For each fixed \(\epsilon\) there is a radius \(r_\epsilon>0\) such that every law in the constrained fixed-support regular model within cell distance \(r_\epsilon\) of \(P_\epsilon\) has the same two strict optimizer assignments and has \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)>\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)/2\).

defs.def:binary-witness: Fix \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=3/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=2\), and let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form \(Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)})\), while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{3/4}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=5/2\), \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=7/2\), \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2\), and \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3\), so the prediction-selected design is genuinely more expensive and \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm p})=B/6<n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm e})=B/5\). For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are \(h_d(l,a)=l/y\) and \(q_d(e,a)=\{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)\}/(1-1/16)\), and the residual prediction variance is \(R(x,y)=(1-x^2)(1-y^2)/(1-x^2y^2)\).
defs.def:regular-law-class: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}=\{P: \text{long- and short-term consistency, observational latent exchangeability and overlap, experimental randomization and overlap, designwise full-short-term external validity and source support hold, and the sequential restriction, both completeness conditions, selection-bridge existence, operator bijectivity, and nondegenerate score variances hold for every }d\in\mathcal D\text{ and }a\in\{0,1\}\}\).
defs.def:predictive-benchmark: Compute \(R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O]\), charge the jointly budget-feasible paired-sample cost through \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=B/(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})\), and minimize the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped objective \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=R_d(P)/n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)/B\) over \(d\in\mathcal D\). Retain all objective minimizers in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\), use a prespecified deterministic order only to implement a tie, and evaluate \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)/\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\).
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-outcomes: \((Y(a),S_{3d}(a))\perp S_{1d}(a)\mid S_{2d}(a),U,X,G=O\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:late-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{3d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:early-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{1d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

snapshot.stmt: For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and fixed \(0<\alpha<1\), as \(B\to\infty\) the floor-count variance of the designwise bridge-functional gradient satisfies \(B\{V_{E,d}/n_{E,B}(d,\alpha)+V_{O,d}/n_{O,B}(d,\alpha)\}=\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)+\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)\), where \(0\le\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)\le 2B^{-1}\{V_{E,d}c_{E,d}^2/\alpha^2+V_{O,d}c_{O,d}^2/(1-\alpha)^2\}\) once \(B\ge2\max\{c_{E,d}/\alpha,c_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\}\). Hence the floor-count variance converges to \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\). The unique minimizer and minimum of this limiting profile are \(\alpha_d^*(P)=\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}/(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})\) and \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2\).  Whenever the designwise bridge functional equals \(\tau\) and the displayed gradient is canonical for \(\tau\), including the binary witness subclass below, the same quantity is the budget-normalized local semiparametric efficiency bound for \(\tau\).

defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\), assume \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), and assume that \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main-study observations used to construct \(\widehat\tau_B\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose that for fixed \(L\), uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(1\le\ell\le L\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{w,h,d}=O_P(\delta_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{2,O,h,d}=O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{w,q,d}=O_P(\delta_{q,B})\), and \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{2,O,q,d}=O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), where all four deterministic rates are \(o(1)\) and \(\min\{\delta_{h,B}\rho_{q,B},\rho_{h,B}\delta_{q,B}\}=o(B^{-1/2})\). Under the full-catalogue pilot law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\) with \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\) with \(r_{\widetilde V,B}=o(1)\). For \(\widehat d_m\) and the feasible share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), form the realized counts \(N_{E,B},N_{O,B}\) and define \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) from the selected foldwise source-score second moments. Then \(B\{V_{E,\widehat d_m}/N_{E,B}+V_{O,\widehat d_m}/N_{O,B}\}-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), \(\widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), and
\[
 \frac{\sqrt B\{\widehat\tau_B-(\mu_{\widehat d_m,1}-\mu_{\widehat d_m,0})\}}
 {\widehat s_B}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
Let \(z_{1-\eta/2}\) be the \((1-\eta/2)\)-quantile of the standard normal law and define
\[
 I_B=\left[
 \widehat\tau_B-z_{1-\eta/2}\frac{\widehat s_B}{\sqrt B},
 \widehat\tau_B+z_{1-\eta/2}\frac{\widehat s_B}{\sqrt B}
 \right].
\]
Then \(P\{\mu_{\widehat d_m,1}-\mu_{\widehat d_m,0}\in I_B\}\to1-\eta\). If, in addition, \(\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}=\tau\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\), then the same studentized limit is centered at \(\tau\) and \(P\{\tau\in I_B\}\to1-\eta\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.
defs.def:selected-wald-variance: For the selected design \(\widehat d_m\) and feasible pilot share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), use the realized counts \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\). For each main-study observation, evaluate its experimental or observational score using \(\widehat h_{\widehat d_m,B}^{(-\ell)}\) and \(\widehat q_{\widehat d_m,B}^{(-\ell)}\) trained outside its fold. Let \(\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}\) and \(\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}\) be the corresponding within-source empirical second moments, and set \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) and \(\widehat s_B=(\widehat s_B^2)^{1/2}\).

assumptions.ass:independent-pilot: \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main-study observations used to construct \(\widehat\tau_B\).
assumptions.ass:main-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.
assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.
assumptions.ass:uniform-outcome-strong-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{2,O,h,d}=O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.
assumptions.ass:uniform-outcome-weak-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{w,h,d}=O_P(\delta_{h,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.
assumptions.ass:uniform-selection-strong-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{2,O,q,d}=O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.
assumptions.ass:uniform-selection-weak-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{w,q,d}=O_P(\delta_{q,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.

snapshot.stmt:
For the unequal-cost binary witness, every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives a law \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) for which both designs identify \(\tau\) and are regular. Although \(d_{\mathrm p}\) is more expensive, with \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=6>5=c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}\), it is the unique minimizer of this paper's Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped paired-source prediction objective, while \(d_{\mathrm e}\) is the unique minimizer of the causal design value. More precisely,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{448}{2025\epsilon^2}+\frac{6272}{2025},\qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)=\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). The same divergence holds on the relatively open range of cap-feasible cost vectors satisfying
\[
 1<\frac{c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}}
 {c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}}<\frac{48}{35},
\]
for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\). Thus the failure is neither an equal-cost artifact nor an identification failure.

defs.def:binary-region:
Fix the catalogue, costs, cap, and the two role assignments exactly as in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\).  Name as the \emph{binary constrained finite-cell model} the family \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}\) of laws \(P\) with constant \(X\) and constant \(S_{2d}\), latent variables \(U,T,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4\in\{-1,1\}\), \(A=(T+1)/2\), and potential variables
\[
 Z(a)=(W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4),\qquad Y(a)=U,qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For strictly positive probability vectors \((\pi_g:g\in\{E,O\})\), \((\nu_u:u\in\{-1,1\})\), \((\lambda_t:t\in\{-1,1\})\), observational treatment kernels \(e_u(t)\), and proxy kernels \(k_{j,u}(w)\), its latent-cell mass factorizes as
\[
 P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
 =\pi_g\nu_u
 \bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t+\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}
 \prod_{j=1}^4 k_{j,u}(w_j).                                    \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(U\) is independent of \(G\), treatment is randomized independently of \(U\) in source \(E\), and the four proxies are mutually independent conditional on \(U\) and invariant across source and treatment.  The design \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \((W_1,W_2)\) to roles one and three, and \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \((W_3,W_4)\) to roles one and three; role two is constant.  The witness \(P_\epsilon\) is the point having \(\pi_E=\pi_O=1/2\), \(\nu_{-1}=\nu_1=1/2\), \(\lambda_{-1}=\lambda_1=1/2\), \(e_u(t)=(1+tu/4)/2\), and
\[
 k_{j,u}(w)=\frac{1+s_juw}{2},
 \qquad (s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4)=(\epsilon,3/4,1/2,1/2).
\]
The model is parameterized by the relative interiors of these finite probability simplices.  Its relative topology is equivalently the Euclidean parameter topology or the maximum-norm topology induced by the complete latent-cell vector in (1).  For every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), let \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{reg}}>0\) be furnished by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}regular\text{-}locus\text{-}relatively\text{-}open}\), and let \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{opt}}>0\) be the optimizer-stability radius furnished by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}witness\text{-}stability}\).  Choose
\[
 0<\delta_\epsilon<\min\{r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{reg}},r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{opt}}\}
\]
and define
\[
 \mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}
 =\bigcup_{0<\epsilon<10^{-3}}
 \left\{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}:
 \|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<\delta_\epsilon\right\}.     \tag{2}
\]
Thus each set in the union is a relative open ball in the named model, and \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is relatively open there.  The regular-neighborhood lemma proves, rather than defines, that \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\).  No claim of openness in the ambient unrestricted probability simplex is made, because the factorization, support, consistency, and causal equality restrictions define a lower-dimensional model.

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(\mathcal D\) be finite and nonempty.  Suppose the costs and population variance components obey
\[
 0<\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\min\{c_{E,d},c_{O,d},V_{E,d},V_{O,d}\}
 \le
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{c_{E,d},c_{O,d},V_{E,d},V_{O,d}\}<\infty.
\]
Suppose
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\bigl\{
 |\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,
 |\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\bigr\}=O_P(r_{V,m}),
 \qquad r_{V,m}=o(1),
 \qquad \underline v_m\downarrow0,
\]
and define \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}\) by the full-catalogue pilot selector.  Then, along every joint sequence \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\),
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}\left|B\left\{
 \frac{V_{E,d}}{\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor}
 +\frac{V_{O,d}}{\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor}
 \right\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)\right|
 =O_P\!\left((r_{V,m}+\underline v_m)^2+B^{-1}\right).
\]
In particular, allocation estimation enters the profiled value only at second order.

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.

snapshot.stmt: For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and fixed \(0<\alpha<1\), as \(B\to\infty\) the floor-count variance of the designwise bridge-functional gradient satisfies \(B\{V_{E,d}/n_{E,B}(d,\alpha)+V_{O,d}/n_{O,B}(d,\alpha)\}=\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)+\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)\), where \(0\le\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)\le 2B^{-1}\{V_{E,d}c_{E,d}^2/\alpha^2+V_{O,d}c_{O,d}^2/(1-\alpha)^2\}\) once \(B\ge2\max\{c_{E,d}/\alpha,c_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\}\). Hence the floor-count variance converges to \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\). The unique minimizer and minimum of this limiting profile are \(\alpha_d^*(P)=\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}/(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})\) and \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2\).  Whenever the designwise bridge functional equals \(\tau\) and the displayed gradient is canonical for \(\tau\), including the binary witness subclass below, the same quantity is the budget-normalized local semiparametric efficiency bound for \(\tau\).

defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).

snapshot.stmt: For the full-catalogue pilot selector, \(0\le\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)-\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\le2\varepsilon_m\) deterministically, and \(\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\subseteq\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\). Thus \(P\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\le P\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\to0\), with the right-hand event empty when every design is optimal. Under \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\), and \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), \(\varepsilon_m=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat\alpha_{d,m}-\alpha_d^*(P)|=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m)\), and uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(B\{V_{E,d}/\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor+V_{O,d}/\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m+B^{-1})=o_P(1)\). The deterministic tie rule selects one empirical minimizer, while consistency means membership in the full population optimizer set \(D^*(P)\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\), assume \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), and assume that \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main-study observations used to construct \(\widehat\tau_B\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose that for fixed \(L\), uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(1\le\ell\le L\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{w,h,d}=O_P(\delta_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{2,O,h,d}=O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{w,q,d}=O_P(\delta_{q,B})\), and \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{2,O,q,d}=O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), where all four deterministic rates are \(o(1)\) and \(\min\{\delta_{h,B}\rho_{q,B},\rho_{h,B}\delta_{q,B}\}=o(B^{-1/2})\). Under the full-catalogue pilot law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\) with \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\) with \(r_{\widetilde V,B}=o(1)\). For \(\widehat d_m\) and the feasible share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), form the realized counts \(N_{E,B},N_{O,B}\) and define \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) from the selected foldwise source-score second moments. Then \(B\{V_{E,\widehat d_m}/N_{E,B}+V_{O,\widehat d_m}/N_{O,B}\}-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), \(\widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), and
\[
 \frac{\sqrt B\{\widehat\tau_B-(\mu_{\widehat d_m,1}-\mu_{\widehat d_m,0})\}}
 {\widehat s_B}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
Let \(z_{1-\eta/2}\) be the \((1-\eta/2)\)-quantile of the standard normal law and define
\[
 I_B=\left[
 \widehat\tau_B-z_{1-\eta/2}\frac{\widehat s_B}{\sqrt B},
 \widehat\tau_B+z_{1-\eta/2}\frac{\widehat s_B}{\sqrt B}
 \right].
\]
Then \(P\{\mu_{\widehat d_m,1}-\mu_{\widehat d_m,0}\in I_B\}\to1-\eta\). If, in addition, \(\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}=\tau\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\), then the same studentized limit is centered at \(\tau\) and \(P\{\tau\in I_B\}\to1-\eta\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.
defs.def:selected-wald-variance: For the selected design \(\widehat d_m\) and feasible pilot share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), use the realized counts \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\). For each main-study observation, evaluate its experimental or observational score using \(\widehat h_{\widehat d_m,B}^{(-\ell)}\) and \(\widehat q_{\widehat d_m,B}^{(-\ell)}\) trained outside its fold. Let \(\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}\) and \(\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}\) be the corresponding within-source empirical second moments, and set \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) and \(\widehat s_B=(\widehat s_B^2)^{1/2}\).

assumptions.ass:independent-pilot: \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main-study observations used to construct \(\widehat\tau_B\).
assumptions.ass:main-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.
assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.
assumptions.ass:uniform-outcome-strong-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{2,O,h,d}=O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.
assumptions.ass:uniform-outcome-weak-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{w,h,d}=O_P(\delta_{h,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.
assumptions.ass:uniform-selection-strong-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{2,O,q,d}=O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.
assumptions.ass:uniform-selection-weak-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{w,q,d}=O_P(\delta_{q,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), if \(\mathcal D=\{d\}\), the main study fixes positive counts \(n_E,n_O\), and \(B=c_{E,d}n_E+c_{O,d}n_O\), then
\[
 \frac{1}{B}\mathcal V_d\!\left(\frac{c_{E,d}n_E}{B};P\right)
 =\frac{V_{E,d}}{n_E}+\frac{V_{O,d}}{n_O}.
\]
The right-hand side is the fixed-system two-source pathwise-gradient variance for the identified observed-data bridge contrast \(\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}\). If, in addition, \(\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}=\tau\) and \((\phi_{E,d},\phi_{O,d})\) is the canonical gradient for \(\tau\) in the Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang fixed-system model under its bridge-existence, bridge-uniqueness, operator-bijectivity, moment, and interior sampling-ratio conditions, then this quantity is their fixed-system causal semiparametric efficiency bound. Without those additional causal-identification and canonical-gradient conditions, only the bridge-functional gradient-variance identity is asserted.

For the unequal-cost binary witness, every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives a law \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) for which both designs identify \(\tau\) and are regular. Although \(d_{\mathrm p}\) is more expensive, with \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=6>5=c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}\), it is the unique minimizer of this paper's Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped paired-source prediction objective, while \(d_{\mathrm e}\) is the unique minimizer of both the paper's arm-normalized profile and the Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang-normalized causal efficiency profile. More precisely,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{448}{2025\epsilon^2}+\frac{6272}{2025},
 \qquad
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},
\]
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). On the relatively open subregion \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\subseteq\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\), every design remains regular and identifies \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)=\infty.
\]
The same center-path divergence, for both ratios, holds on the relatively open range of cap-feasible cost vectors satisfying
\[
 1<\frac{c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}}
 {c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}}<\frac{48}{35},
\]
for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\). Thus the failure is neither an equal-cost artifact nor an identification failure, and the absolute causal-efficiency interpretation uses the IKM-normalized profile rather than the unscaled arm-normalized profile.

defs.def:binary-region:
Fix the catalogue, costs, cap, and the two role assignments exactly as in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\).  Name as the \emph{binary constrained finite-cell model} the family \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}\) of laws \(P\) with constant \(X\) and constant \(S_{2d}\), latent variables \(U,T,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4\in\{-1,1\}\), \(A=(T+1)/2\), and potential variables
\[
 Z(a)=(W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4),\qquad Y(a)=U,qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For strictly positive probability vectors \((\pi_g:g\in\{E,O\})\), \((\nu_u:u\in\{-1,1\})\), \((\lambda_t:t\in\{-1,1\})\), observational treatment kernels \(e_u(t)\), and proxy kernels \(k_{j,u}(w)\), its latent-cell mass factorizes as
\[
 P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
 =\pi_g\nu_u
 \bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t+\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}
 \prod_{j=1}^4 k_{j,u}(w_j).                                    \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(U\) is independent of \(G\), treatment is randomized independently of \(U\) in source \(E\), and the four proxies are mutually independent conditional on \(U\) and invariant across source and treatment.  The design \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \((W_1,W_2)\) to roles one and three, and \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \((W_3,W_4)\) to roles one and three; role two is constant.  The witness \(P_\epsilon\) is the point having \(\pi_E=\pi_O=1/2\), \(\nu_{-1}=\nu_1=1/2\), \(\lambda_{-1}=\lambda_1=1/2\), \(e_u(t)=(1+tu/4)/2\), and
\[
 k_{j,u}(w)=\frac{1+s_juw}{2},
 \qquad (s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4)=(\epsilon,3/4,1/2,1/2).
\]
The model is parameterized by the relative interiors of these finite probability simplices.  Its relative topology is equivalently the Euclidean parameter topology or the maximum-norm topology induced by the complete latent-cell vector in (1).  For every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), let \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{reg}}>0\) be furnished by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}regular\text{-}locus\text{-}relatively\text{-}open}\), and let \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{opt}}>0\) be the optimizer-stability radius furnished by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}witness\text{-}stability}\).  Choose
\[
 0<\delta_\epsilon<\min\{r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{reg}},r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{opt}}\}
\]
and define
\[
 \mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}
 =\bigcup_{0<\epsilon<10^{-3}}
 \left\{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}:
 \|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<\delta_\epsilon\right\}.     \tag{2}
\]
Thus each set in the union is a relative open ball in the named model, and \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is relatively open there.  The regular-neighborhood lemma proves, rather than defines, that \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\).  No claim of openness in the ambient unrestricted probability simplex is made, because the factorization, support, consistency, and causal equality restrictions define a lower-dimensional model.
defs.def:binary-witness: Fix \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=3/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=2\), and let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form \(Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)})\), while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{3/4}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=5/2\), \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=7/2\), \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2\), and \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3\), so the prediction-selected design is genuinely more expensive and \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm p})=B/6<n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm e})=B/5\). For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are \(h_d(l,a)=l/y\) and \(q_d(e,a)=\{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)\}/(1-1/16)\), and the residual prediction variance is \(R(x,y)=(1-x^2)(1-y^2)/(1-x^2y^2)\).
defs.def:regular-law-class: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}=\{P: \text{long- and short-term consistency, observational latent exchangeability and overlap, experimental randomization and overlap, designwise full-short-term external validity and source support hold, and the sequential restriction, both completeness conditions, selection-bridge existence, operator bijectivity, and nondegenerate score variances hold for every }d\in\mathcal D\text{ and }a\in\{0,1\}\}\).
defs.def:predictive-benchmark: Compute \(R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O]\), charge the jointly budget-feasible paired-sample cost through \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=B/(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})\), and minimize the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped objective \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=R_d(P)/n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)/B\) over \(d\in\mathcal D\). Retain all objective minimizers in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\), use a prespecified deterministic order only to implement a tie, and evaluate \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)/\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\).
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-outcomes: \((Y(a),S_{3d}(a))\perp S_{1d}(a)\mid S_{2d}(a),U,X,G=O\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:late-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{3d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), the exact fixed-catalogue diagnostic identity is
\[
 1\le\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d'}V_{E,d'}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d'}V_{O,d'}})^2}<\infty.
\]
The smallest constant in the actual best-tie inequality is exactly \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\). The least constant that makes every pairwise implication
\(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)\Rightarrow \mathcal V_d^*(P)\le C(P)\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\)
valid is
\[
 \max_{\substack{d,d'\in\mathcal D:\,
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)}}
 \frac{\mathcal V_d^*(P)}{\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
Every displayed constant is finite at a fixed \(P\), but \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). Thus finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) yields an exact law-specific enumeration, not a primitive uniform predictive-efficiency guarantee.

defs.def:predictive-benchmark: Compute \(R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O]\), charge the jointly budget-feasible paired-sample cost through \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=B/(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})\), and minimize the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped objective \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=R_d(P)/n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)/B\) over \(d\in\mathcal D\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).

snapshot.stmt:
For the unequal-cost binary construction, every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives \(P_{\epsilon}\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), the predictive optimizer is \(d_{\mathrm p}\), and the design-value optimizer is \(d_{\mathrm e}\).  Moreover,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{448}{2025\epsilon^2}+\frac{6272}{2025},\qquad
 \mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e}}^*(P_{\epsilon})=\frac{3872}{25},\qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\epsilon})=\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
For each fixed \(\epsilon\) there is a radius \(r_\epsilon>0\) such that every law in the constrained fixed-support regular model within cell distance \(r_\epsilon\) of \(P_\epsilon\) has the same two strict optimizer assignments and has \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)>\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)/2\).

defs.def:binary-witness: Fix \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=3/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=2\), and let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form \(Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)})\), while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{3/4}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=5/2\), \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=7/2\), \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2\), and \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3\), so the prediction-selected design is genuinely more expensive and \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm p})=B/6<n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm e})=B/5\). For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are \(h_d(l,a)=l/y\) and \(q_d(e,a)=\{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)\}/(1-1/16)\), and the residual prediction variance is \(R(x,y)=(1-x^2)(1-y^2)/(1-x^2y^2)\).

snapshot.stmt:
Under the IKM score and profile normalization, every binary center law satisfies
\[
 \psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac12\phi_{E,d},
 \qquad
 \psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac12\phi_{O,d},
 \qquad
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},
 \qquad
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon)
\]
for \(g\in\{E,O\}\) and \(d\in\mathcal D\). Consequently \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon)=\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)\). For each fixed \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), there is \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}>0\) such that every law \(P\) in the binary constrained finite-cell model with \(\|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) is regular, both admissible bridge contrasts equal \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 >\frac12\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon).
\]
On this neighborhood, the IKM-normalized profile is the profiled local causal semiparametric efficiency bound under the fixed-system conditions in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\).

snapshot.stmt: For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and fixed \(0<\alpha<1\), as \(B\to\infty\) the floor-count variance of the designwise bridge-functional gradient satisfies \(B\{V_{E,d}/n_{E,B}(d,\alpha)+V_{O,d}/n_{O,B}(d,\alpha)\}=\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)+\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)\), where \(0\le\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)\le 2B^{-1}\{V_{E,d}c_{E,d}^2/\alpha^2+V_{O,d}c_{O,d}^2/(1-\alpha)^2\}\) once \(B\ge2\max\{c_{E,d}/\alpha,c_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\}\). Hence the floor-count variance converges to \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\). The unique minimizer and minimum of this limiting profile are \(\alpha_d^*(P)=\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}/(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})\) and \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2\).  Whenever the designwise bridge functional equals \(\tau\) and the displayed gradient is canonical for \(\tau\), the same quantity is the budget-normalized local semiparametric efficiency bound for \(\tau\).

snapshot.stmt: For the full-catalogue pilot selector, \(0\le\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)-\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\le2\varepsilon_m\) deterministically, and \(\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\subseteq\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\). Thus \(P\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\le P\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\to0\), with the right-hand event empty when every design is optimal. Under \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\), and \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), \(\varepsilon_m=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat\alpha_{d,m}-\alpha_d^*(P)|=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m)\), and uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(B\{V_{E,d}/\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor+V_{O,d}/\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m+B^{-1})=o_P(1)\). The deterministic tie rule selects one empirical minimizer, while consistency means membership in the full population optimizer set \(D^*(P)\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.

Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).

assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\), assume \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), and assume that \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main-study observations used to construct \(\widehat\tau_B\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose that for fixed \(L\), uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(1\le\ell\le L\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{w,h,d}=O_P(\delta_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{2,O,h,d}=O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{w,q,d}=O_P(\delta_{q,B})\), and \(\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{2,O,q,d}=O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), where all four deterministic rates are \(o(1)\) and \(\min\{\delta_{h,B}\rho_{q,B},\rho_{h,B}\delta_{q,B}\}=o(B^{-1/2})\). Under the full-catalogue pilot law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\) with \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\). Under the joint main-study law, suppose \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\) with \(r_{\widetilde V,B}=o(1)\). For \(\widehat d_m\) and the feasible share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), form the realized counts \(N_{E,B},N_{O,B}\) and define \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) from the selected foldwise source-score second moments. Then \(B\{V_{E,\widehat d_m}/N_{E,B}+V_{O,\widehat d_m}/N_{O,B}\}-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), \(\widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1)\), and
\[
 \frac{\sqrt B\{\widehat\tau_B-(\mu_{\widehat d_m,1}-\mu_{\widehat d_m,0})\}}
 {\widehat s_B}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
Let \(z_{1-\eta/2}\) be the \((1-\eta/2)\)-quantile of the standard normal law and define
\[
 I_B=\left[
 \widehat\tau_B-z_{1-\eta/2}\frac{\widehat s_B}{\sqrt B},
 \widehat\tau_B+z_{1-\eta/2}\frac{\widehat s_B}{\sqrt B}
 \right].
\]
Then \(P\{\mu_{\widehat d_m,1}-\mu_{\widehat d_m,0}\in I_B\}\to1-\eta\). If, in addition, \(\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}=\tau\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\), then the same studentized limit is centered at \(\tau\) and \(P\{\tau\in I_B\}\to1-\eta\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.
defs.def:selected-wald-variance: For the selected design \(\widehat d_m\) and feasible pilot share \(\widehat\alpha_m\), use the realized counts \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\). For each main-study observation, evaluate its experimental or observational score using \(\widehat h_{\widehat d_m,B}^{(-\ell)}\) and \(\widehat q_{\widehat d_m,B}^{(-\ell)}\) trained outside its fold. Let \(\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}\) and \(\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}\) be the corresponding within-source empirical second moments, and set \(\widehat s_B^2=B\{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{E,B}+\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}/N_{O,B}\}\) and \(\widehat s_B=(\widehat s_B^2)^{1/2}\).

assumptions.ass:independent-pilot: \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main-study observations used to construct \(\widehat\tau_B\).
assumptions.ass:main-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.
assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.
assumptions.ass:uniform-outcome-strong-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{2,O,h,d}=O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.
assumptions.ass:uniform-outcome-weak-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{w,h,d}=O_P(\delta_{h,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.
assumptions.ass:uniform-selection-strong-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{2,O,q,d}=O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.
assumptions.ass:uniform-selection-weak-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{w,q,d}=O_P(\delta_{q,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), if \(\mathcal D=\{d\}\), the main study fixes positive counts \(n_E,n_O\), and \(B=c_{E,d}n_E+c_{O,d}n_O\), then
\[
 \frac{1}{B}\mathcal V_d\!\left(\frac{c_{E,d}n_E}{B};P\right)
 =\frac{V_{E,d}}{n_E}+\frac{V_{O,d}}{n_O}.
\]
The right-hand side is the fixed-system two-source pathwise-gradient variance for the identified observed-data bridge contrast \(\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}\). If, in addition, \(\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}=\tau\) and \((\phi_{E,d},\phi_{O,d})\) is the canonical gradient for \(\tau\) in the Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang fixed-system model under its bridge-existence, bridge-uniqueness, operator-bijectivity, moment, and interior sampling-ratio conditions, then this quantity is their fixed-system causal semiparametric efficiency bound. Without those additional causal-identification and canonical-gradient conditions, only the bridge-functional gradient-variance identity is asserted.

For the unequal-cost binary witness, every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives a law \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) for which both designs identify \(\tau\) and are regular. Although \(d_{\mathrm p}\) is more expensive, with \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=6>5=c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}\), it is the unique minimizer of this paper's Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped paired-source prediction objective, while \(d_{\mathrm e}\) is the unique minimizer of both the paper's arm-normalized profile and the Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang-normalized causal efficiency profile. More precisely,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{448}{2025\epsilon^2}+\frac{6272}{2025},
 \qquad
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},
\]
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). On the relatively open subregion \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\subseteq\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\), every design remains regular and identifies \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)=\infty.
\]
The same center-path divergence, for both ratios, holds on the relatively open range of cap-feasible cost vectors satisfying
\[
 1<\frac{c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}}
 {c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}}<\frac{48}{35},
\]
for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\). Thus the failure is neither an equal-cost artifact nor an identification failure, and the absolute causal-efficiency interpretation uses the IKM-normalized profile rather than the unscaled arm-normalized profile.

defs.def:binary-region:
Fix the catalogue, costs, cap, and the two role assignments exactly as in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\).  Name as the \emph{binary constrained finite-cell model} the family \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}\) of laws \(P\) with constant \(X\) and constant \(S_{2d}\), latent variables \(U,T,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4\in\{-1,1\}\), \(A=(T+1)/2\), and potential variables
\[
 Z(a)=(W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4),\qquad Y(a)=U,qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For strictly positive probability vectors \((\pi_g:g\in\{E,O\})\), \((\nu_u:u\in\{-1,1\})\), \((\lambda_t:t\in\{-1,1\})\), observational treatment kernels \(e_u(t)\), and proxy kernels \(k_{j,u}(w)\), its latent-cell mass factorizes as
\[
 P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
 =\pi_g\nu_u
 \bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t+\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}
 \prod_{j=1}^4 k_{j,u}(w_j).                                    \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(U\) is independent of \(G\), treatment is randomized independently of \(U\) in source \(E\), and the four proxies are mutually independent conditional on \(U\) and invariant across source and treatment.  The design \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \((W_1,W_2)\) to roles one and three, and \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \((W_3,W_4)\) to roles one and three; role two is constant.  The witness \(P_\epsilon\) is the point having \(\pi_E=\pi_O=1/2\), \(\nu_{-1}=\nu_1=1/2\), \(\lambda_{-1}=\lambda_1=1/2\), \(e_u(t)=(1+tu/4)/2\), and
\[
 k_{j,u}(w)=\frac{1+s_juw}{2},
 \qquad (s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4)=(\epsilon,3/4,1/2,1/2).
\]
The model is parameterized by the relative interiors of these finite probability simplices.  Its relative topology is equivalently the Euclidean parameter topology or the maximum-norm topology induced by the complete latent-cell vector in (1).  For every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), let \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{reg}}>0\) be furnished by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}regular\text{-}locus\text{-}relatively\text{-}open}\), and let \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{opt}}>0\) be the optimizer-stability radius furnished by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}witness\text{-}stability}\).  Choose
\[
 0<\delta_\epsilon<\min\{r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{reg}},r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{opt}}\}
\]
and define
\[
 \mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}
 =\bigcup_{0<\epsilon<10^{-3}}
 \left\{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}:
 \|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<\delta_\epsilon\right\}.     \tag{2}
\]
Thus each set in the union is a relative open ball in the named model, and \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is relatively open there.  The regular-neighborhood lemma proves, rather than defines, that \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\).  No claim of openness in the ambient unrestricted probability simplex is made, because the factorization, support, consistency, and causal equality restrictions define a lower-dimensional model.
defs.def:binary-witness: Fix \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=3/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=2\), and let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form \(Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)})\), while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{3/4}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=5/2\), \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=7/2\), \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2\), and \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3\), so the prediction-selected design is genuinely more expensive and \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm p})=B/6<n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm e})=B/5\). For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are \(h_d(l,a)=l/y\) and \(q_d(e,a)=\{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)\}/(1-1/16)\), and the residual prediction variance is \(R(x,y)=(1-x^2)(1-y^2)/(1-x^2y^2)\).
defs.def:regular-law-class: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}=\{P: \text{long- and short-term consistency, observational latent exchangeability and overlap, experimental randomization and overlap, designwise full-short-term external validity and source support hold, and the sequential restriction, both completeness conditions, selection-bridge existence, operator bijectivity, and nondegenerate score variances hold for every }d\in\mathcal D\text{ and }a\in\{0,1\}\}\).
defs.def:predictive-benchmark: Compute \(R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O]\), charge the jointly budget-feasible paired-sample cost through \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=B/(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})\), and minimize the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped objective \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=R_d(P)/n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)/B\) over \(d\in\mathcal D\). Retain all objective minimizers in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\), use a prespecified deterministic order only to implement a tie, and evaluate \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)/\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\).
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-outcomes: \((Y(a),S_{3d}(a))\perp S_{1d}(a)\mid S_{2d}(a),U,X,G=O\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:late-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{3d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:early-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{1d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

Let \(\mathcal D\) be finite and nonempty.  Suppose the costs and population variance components obey
\[
 0<\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\min\{c_{E,d},c_{O,d},V_{E,d},V_{O,d}\}
 \le
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{c_{E,d},c_{O,d},V_{E,d},V_{O,d}\}<\infty.
\]
Suppose
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\bigl\{
 |\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,
 |\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\bigr\}=O_P(r_{V,m}),
 \qquad r_{V,m}=o(1),
 \qquad \underline v_m\downarrow0,
\]
and define \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}\) by the full-catalogue pilot selector.  Then, along every joint sequence \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\),
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}\left|B\left\{
 \frac{V_{E,d}}{\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor}
 +\frac{V_{O,d}}{\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor}
 \right\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)\right|
 =O_P\!\left((r_{V,m}+\underline v_m)^2+B^{-1}\right).
\]

Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), the exact fixed-catalogue diagnostic identity is
\[
 1\le\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d'}V_{E,d'}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d'}V_{O,d'}})^2}<\infty.
\]
The smallest constant in the actual best-tie inequality is exactly \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\). The least constant that makes every pairwise implication
\(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)\Rightarrow \mathcal V_d^*(P)\le C(P)\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\)
valid is
\[
 \max_{\substack{d,d'\in\mathcal D:\,
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)}}
 \frac{\mathcal V_d^*(P)}{\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
Every displayed constant is finite at a fixed \(P\), but \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). Thus finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) yields an exact law-specific enumeration, not a primitive uniform predictive-efficiency guarantee.

Under the IKM score and profile normalization, every binary center law satisfies
\[
 \psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac12\phi_{E,d},
 \qquad
 \psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac12\phi_{O,d},
 \qquad
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},
 \qquad
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon)
\]
for \(g\in\{E,O\}\) and \(d\in\mathcal D\). Consequently \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon)=\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)\). \[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 >\frac12\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon).
\]

defs.def:ikmw-normalized-design-value:
For each regular design \(d\), define the source scores on the Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang normalization by
\[
 \psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{E,1})\phi_{E,d},
 \qquad
 \psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{O,1})\phi_{O,d},
\]
and define their source-conditional second moments by
\[
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=E]
 =(1-p_{E,1})^2V_{E,d},
\]
\[
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=O]
 =(1-p_{O,1})^2V_{O,d}.
\]
