\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
 =\left(
 \sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 +\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \right)^2,
\]
\[
 D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
 =\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d',\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}.
\]

For the full-catalogue pilot selector, \(0\le\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)-\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\le2\varepsilon_m\) deterministically, and \(\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\subseteq\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\). Thus \(P\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\le P\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\to0\), with the right-hand event empty when every design is optimal. Under \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\), and \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), \(\varepsilon_m=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat\alpha_{d,m}-\alpha_d^*(P)|=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m)\), and uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\), after assigning the entire floor-count brace the value zero whenever either floor count is zero,
\[
B\left\{\frac{V_{E,d}}{\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor}+\frac{V_{O,d}}{\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor}\right\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m+B^{-1})=o_P(1).
\]
The deterministic tie rule selects one empirical minimizer, while consistency means membership in the full population optimizer set \(D^*(P)\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.

snapshot.stmt:
For the unequal-cost binary witness, every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives a law \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) for which both designs identify \(\tau\) and are regular. Although \(d_{\mathrm p}\) is more expensive, with \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=6>5=c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}\), it is the unique minimizer of this paper's Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped paired-source prediction objective, while \(d_{\mathrm e}\) is the unique minimizer of both the paper's arm-normalized profile and the Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang-normalized causal efficiency profile. More precisely,
\[
V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{448}{2025\epsilon^2}+\frac{6272}{2025},
\qquad V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
\qquad V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},
\]
\[
\mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)=\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon),
\qquad
\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon)=\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)=\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). On the relatively open subregion \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\subseteq\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\), every design remains regular and identifies \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)=\infty.
\]
The same center-path divergence, for both ratios, holds for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\) on the relatively open subset of the induced cap-feasible catalogue-cost manifold
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal C_\kappa=\biggl\{(b_E,b_O,c_1,\ldots,c_K):{}&0<b_E<b_O,\quad c_j>0,\\
&\sum_{j\in M_d}c_j\le\kappa\quad(d\in\mathcal D),\\
&c_{E,d}=b_E+\sum_{j\in M_d}c_j,\quad
c_{O,d}=b_O+\sum_{j\in M_d}c_j\quad(d\in\mathcal D)\biggr\}
\end{aligned}
\]
on which
\[
1<\frac{c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}}{c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}}<\frac{48}{35}.
\]
Thus the failure is neither an equal-cost artifact nor an identification failure, and the absolute causal-efficiency interpretation uses the IKM-normalized profile rather than the unscaled arm-normalized profile.

defs.def:binary-ikmw-region:
For every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), let \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}>0\) be furnished by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}stability}\), and let \(\delta_\epsilon\) be the radius used in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}region}\). Choose
\[
 0<\widetilde\delta_\epsilon
 <\min\{\delta_\epsilon,r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}\}
\]
and define the relatively open normalized-efficiency witness region
\[
 \mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\bigcup_{0<\epsilon<10^{-3}}
 \left\{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}:
 \|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<\widetilde\delta_\epsilon\right\}.
\]
defs.def:binary-region:
Fix the catalogue, costs, cap, and the two role assignments exactly as in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\). Name as the \emph{binary constrained finite-cell model} the family \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}\) of laws \(P\) with constant \(X\) and constant \(S_{2d}\), latent variables \(U,T,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4\in\{-1,1\}\), \(A=(T+1)/2\), and potential variables
\[
Z(a)=(W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4),\qquad Y(a)=U,\qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For strictly positive probability vectors \((\pi_g:g\in\{E,O\})\), \((\nu_u:u\in\{-1,1\})\), \((\lambda_t:t\in\{-1,1\})\), observational treatment kernels \(e_u(t)\), and proxy kernels \(k_{j,u}(w)\), its latent-cell mass factorizes as
\[
P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
=\pi_g\nu_u\bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t+\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}
\prod_{j=1}^4k_{j,u}(w_j). \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(U\) is independent of \(G\), treatment is randomized independently of \(U\) in source \(E\), and the four proxies are mutually independent conditional on \(U\) and invariant across source and treatment. The design \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \((W_1,W_2)\) to roles one and three, and \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \((W_3,W_4)\) to roles one and three; role two is constant. The witness \(P_\epsilon\) is the point having \(\pi_E=\pi_O=1/2\), \(\nu_{-1}=\nu_1=1/2\), \(\lambda_{-1}=\lambda_1=1/2\), \(e_u(t)=(1+tu/4)/2\), and
\[
k_{j,u}(w)=\frac{1+s_juw}{2},
\qquad(s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4)=(\epsilon,3/4,1/2,1/2).
\]
The model is parameterized by the relative interiors of these finite probability simplices. Its relative topology is equivalently the Euclidean parameter topology or the maximum-norm topology induced by the complete latent-cell vector in (1). For every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), let \(r_\epsilon>0\) be furnished by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}witness\text{-}stability}\), and set \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{opt}}:=r_\epsilon\). Choose \(0<\delta_\epsilon<r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{opt}}\) and define
\[
\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}=\bigcup_{0<\epsilon<10^{-3}}
\left\{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}:
\|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<\delta_\epsilon\right\}. \tag{2}
\]
Each member of every ball is regular and retains the two strict optimizer assignments by the cited stability lemma. Thus \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) and is relatively open in the named constrained finite-cell model. No claim of openness in the ambient unrestricted probability simplex is made, because the factorization, support, consistency, and causal equality restrictions define a lower-dimensional model.
defs.def:binary-witness: Fix \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=3/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=2\), and let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form \(Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)})\), while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{3/4}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=5/2\), \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=7/2\), \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2\), and \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3\), so the prediction-selected design is genuinely more expensive and \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm p})=B/6<n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm e})=B/5\). For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are \(h_d(l,a)=l/y\) and \(q_d(e,a)=\{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)\}/(1-1/16)\), and the residual prediction variance is \(R(x,y)=(1-x^2)(1-y^2)/(1-x^2y^2)\).
defs.def:regular-law-class: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}=\{P: \text{long- and short-term consistency, observational latent exchangeability and overlap, experimental randomization and overlap, designwise full-short-term external validity and source support hold, and the sequential restriction, both completeness conditions, selection-bridge existence, operator bijectivity, and nondegenerate score variances hold for every }d\in\mathcal D\text{ and }a\in\{0,1\}\}\).
defs.def:predictive-benchmark: Compute \(R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O]\), charge the jointly budget-feasible paired-sample cost through \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=B/(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})\), and minimize the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped objective \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=R_d(P)/n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)/B\) over \(d\in\mathcal D\). Retain all objective minimizers in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\), use a prespecified deterministic order only to implement a tie, and evaluate \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)/\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\).
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.
defs.def:ikmw-normalized-design-value:
For each regular design \(d\), define the source scores on the Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang normalization by
\[
 \psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{E,1})\phi_{E,d},
 \qquad
 \psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{O,1})\phi_{O,d},
\]
and define their source-conditional second moments by
\[
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=E]
 =(1-p_{E,1})^2V_{E,d},
\]
\[
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=O]
 =(1-p_{O,1})^2V_{O,d}.
\]
The profiled IKM-normalized value, its optimizer set, and the best-tie predictive approximation ratio are
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
 =\left(
 \sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 +\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \right)^2,
\]
\[
 D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
 =\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d',\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}.
\]
These objects are defined only as normalization-specific score moments and profiles. Their interpretation as causal efficiency bounds is supplied design by design by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\) after its causal-identification and regularity premises have been verified.

assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-outcomes: \((Y(a),S_{3d}(a))\perp S_{1d}(a)\mid S_{2d}(a),U,X,G=O\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:late-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{3d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:early-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{1d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(\mathcal D\) be finite and nonempty. Suppose the costs and population variance components obey
\[
0<\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\min\{c_{E,d},c_{O,d},V_{E,d},V_{O,d}\}
\le
\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{c_{E,d},c_{O,d},V_{E,d},V_{O,d}\}<\infty.
\]
Suppose
\[
\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\bigl\{
|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,
|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\bigr\}=O_P(r_{V,m}),
\qquad r_{V,m}=o(1),
\qquad \underline v_m\downarrow0,
\]
and define \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}\) by the full-catalogue pilot selector. For every \(d\) inside the following maximum, assign the entire floor-count expression the value zero whenever either floor count is zero. Then, along every joint sequence \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\),
\[
\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\left|B\left\{
\frac{V_{E,d}}{\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor}
+\frac{V_{O,d}}{\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor}
\right\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)\right|
=O_P\!\left((r_{V,m}+\underline v_m)^2+B^{-1}\right).
\]
In particular, allocation estimation enters the profiled value only at second order.

Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.

snapshot.stmt:
For the unequal-cost binary construction, every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives \(P_{\epsilon}\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), the predictive optimizer is \(d_{\mathrm p}\), and the design-value optimizer is \(d_{\mathrm e}\).  Moreover,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{448}{2025\epsilon^2}+\frac{6272}{2025},\qquad

 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\epsilon})=\frac{49}{9801\epsilon^2}+O(\epsilon^{-1}).

assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).

snapshot.stmt:
Under the IKM score and profile normalization, every binary center law satisfies
\[
 \psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac12\phi_{E,d},
 \qquad
 \psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac12\phi_{O,d},
 \qquad
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},
 \qquad
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon)
\]
for \(g\in\{E,O\}\) and \(d\in\mathcal D\). Consequently \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon)=\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)\). For each fixed \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), there is \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}>0\) such that every law \(P\) in the binary constrained finite-cell model with \(\|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) is regular, both admissible bridge contrasts equal \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 >\frac12\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon).
\]
On this neighborhood, the IKM-normalized profile is the profiled local causal semiparametric efficiency bound under the fixed-system conditions in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\).

defs.def:binary-witness: Fix \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=3/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=2\), and let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form \(Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)})\), while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{3/4}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=5/2\), \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=7/2\), \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2\), and \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3\), so the prediction-selected design is genuinely more expensive and \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm p})=B/6<n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm e})=B/5\). For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are \(h_d(l,a)=l/y\) and \(q_d(e,a)=\{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)\}/(1-1/16)\), and the residual prediction variance is \(R(x,y)=(1-x^2)(1-y^2)/(1-x^2y^2)\).
defs.def:regular-law-class: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}=\{P: \text{long- and short-term consistency, observational latent exchangeability and overlap, experimental randomization and overlap, designwise full-short-term external validity and source support hold, and the sequential restriction, both completeness conditions, selection-bridge existence, operator bijectivity, and nondegenerate score variances hold for every }d\in\mathcal D\text{ and }a\in\{0,1\}\}\).
defs.def:predictive-benchmark: Compute \(R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O]\), charge the jointly budget-feasible paired-sample cost through \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=B/(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})\), and minimize the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped objective \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=R_d(P)/n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)/B\) over \(d\in\mathcal D\). Retain all objective minimizers in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\), use a prespecified deterministic order only to implement a tie, and evaluate \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)/\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\).
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.
defs.def:ikmw-normalized-design-value:
For each regular design \(d\), define the source scores on the Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang normalization by
\[
 \psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{E,1})\phi_{E,d},
 \qquad
 \psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{O,1})\phi_{O,d},
\]
and define their source-conditional second moments by
\[
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=E]
 =(1-p_{E,1})^2V_{E,d},
\]
\[
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=O]
 =(1-p_{O,1})^2V_{O,d}.
\]
The profiled IKM-normalized value, its optimizer set, and the best-tie predictive approximation ratio are
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
 =\left(
 \sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 +\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \right)^2,
\]
\[
 D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
 =\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d',\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}.
\]
These objects are defined only as normalization-specific score moments and profiles. Their interpretation as causal efficiency bounds is supplied design by design by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\) after its causal-identification and regularity premises have been verified.

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(\mathcal D\) be finite and nonempty. Suppose the costs and population variance components obey
\[
0<\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\min\{c_{E,d},c_{O,d},V_{E,d},V_{O,d}\}
\le
\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{c_{E,d},c_{O,d},V_{E,d},V_{O,d}\}<\infty.
\]
Suppose
\[
\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\bigl\{
|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,
|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\bigr\}=O_P(r_{V,m}),
\qquad r_{V,m}=o(1),
\qquad \underline v_m\downarrow0,
\]
and define \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}\) by the full-catalogue pilot selector. For every \(d\) inside the following maximum, assign the entire floor-count expression the value zero whenever either floor count is zero. Then, along every joint sequence \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\),
\[
\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\left|B\left\{
\frac{V_{E,d}}{\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor}
+\frac{V_{O,d}}{\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor}
\right\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)\right|
=O_P\!\left((r_{V,m}+\underline v_m)^2+B^{-1}\right).
\]
In particular, allocation estimation enters the profiled value only at second order.

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), the exact fixed-catalogue diagnostic identity is
\[
 1\le\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d'}V_{E,d'}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d'}V_{O,d'}})^2}<\infty.
\]
The smallest constant in the actual best-tie inequality is exactly \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\). The least constant that makes every pairwise implication
\(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)\Rightarrow \mathcal V_d^*(P)\le C(P)\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\)
valid is
\[
 \max_{\substack{d,d'\in\mathcal D:\,
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)}}
 \frac{\mathcal V_d^*(P)}{\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
Every displayed constant is finite at a fixed \(P\), but \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\). Thus finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) yields an exact law-specific enumeration, not a primitive uniform predictive-efficiency guarantee.

defs.def:binary-region:
Fix the catalogue, costs, cap, and the two role assignments exactly as in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\). Name as the \emph{binary constrained finite-cell model} the family \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}\) of laws \(P\) with constant \(X\) and constant \(S_{2d}\), latent variables \(U,T,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4\in\{-1,1\}\), \(A=(T+1)/2\), and potential variables
\[
Z(a)=(W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4),\qquad Y(a)=U,\qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For strictly positive probability vectors \((\pi_g:g\in\{E,O\})\), \((\nu_u:u\in\{-1,1\})\), \((\lambda_t:t\in\{-1,1\})\), observational treatment kernels \(e_u(t)\), and proxy kernels \(k_{j,u}(w)\), its latent-cell mass factorizes as
\[
P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
=\pi_g\nu_u\bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t+\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}
\prod_{j=1}^4k_{j,u}(w_j). \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(U\) is independent of \(G\), treatment is randomized independently of \(U\) in source \(E\), and the four proxies are mutually independent conditional on \(U\) and invariant across source and treatment. The design \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \((W_1,W_2)\) to roles one and three, and \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \((W_3,W_4)\) to roles one and three; role two is constant. The witness \(P_\epsilon\) is the point having \(\pi_E=\pi_O=1/2\), \(\nu_{-1}=\nu_1=1/2\), \(\lambda_{-1}=\lambda_1=1/2\), \(e_u(t)=(1+tu/4)/2\), and
\[
k_{j,u}(w)=\frac{1+s_juw}{2},
\qquad(s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4)=(\epsilon,3/4,1/2,1/2).
\]
The model is parameterized by the relative interiors of these finite probability simplices. Its relative topology is equivalently the Euclidean parameter topology or the maximum-norm topology induced by the complete latent-cell vector in (1). For every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), let \(r_\epsilon>0\) be furnished by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}witness\text{-}stability}\), and set \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{opt}}:=r_\epsilon\). Choose \(0<\delta_\epsilon<r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{opt}}\) and define
\[
\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}=\bigcup_{0<\epsilon<10^{-3}}
\left\{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}:
\|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<\delta_\epsilon\right\}. \tag{2}
\]
Each member of every ball is regular and retains the two strict optimizer assignments by the cited stability lemma. Thus \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) and is relatively open in the named constrained finite-cell model. No claim of openness in the ambient unrestricted probability simplex is made, because the factorization, support, consistency, and causal equality restrictions define a lower-dimensional model.

For the unequal-cost binary construction, every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\) gives \(P_{\epsilon}\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), the predictive optimizer is \(d_{\mathrm p}\), and the design-value optimizer is \(d_{\mathrm e}\).  Moreover,
\[

defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-outcomes: \((Y(a),S_{3d}(a))\perp S_{1d}(a)\mid S_{2d}(a),U,X,G=O\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:late-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{3d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:early-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{1d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

snapshot.stmt:
Under the IKM score and profile normalization, every binary center law satisfies
\[
 \psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac12\phi_{E,d},
 \qquad
 \psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac12\phi_{O,d},
 \qquad
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},
 \qquad
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon)
\]
for \(g\in\{E,O\}\) and \(d\in\mathcal D\). Consequently \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon)=\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)\). For each fixed \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), there is \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}>0\) such that every law \(P\) in the binary constrained finite-cell model with \(\|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) is regular, both admissible bridge contrasts equal \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 >\frac12\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon).
\]
On this neighborhood, the IKM-normalized profile is the profiled local causal semiparametric efficiency bound under the fixed-system conditions in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\).

defs.def:binary-witness: Fix \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=3/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=2\), and let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form \(Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{3/4},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)})\), while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{3/4}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=5/2\), \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=7/2\), \(c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2\), and \(c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3\), so the prediction-selected design is genuinely more expensive and \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm p})=B/6<n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d_{\mathrm e})=B/5\). For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are \(h_d(l,a)=l/y\) and \(q_d(e,a)=\{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)\}/(1-1/16)\), and the residual prediction variance is \(R(x,y)=(1-x^2)(1-y^2)/(1-x^2y^2)\).
defs.def:regular-law-class: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}=\{P: \text{long- and short-term consistency, observational latent exchangeability and overlap, experimental randomization and overlap, designwise full-short-term external validity and source support hold, and the sequential restriction, both completeness conditions, selection-bridge existence, operator bijectivity, and nondegenerate score variances hold for every }d\in\mathcal D\text{ and }a\in\{0,1\}\}\).
defs.def:predictive-benchmark: Compute \(R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O]\), charge the jointly budget-feasible paired-sample cost through \(n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=B/(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})\), and minimize the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm-shaped objective \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=R_d(P)/n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)/B\) over \(d\in\mathcal D\). Retain all objective minimizers in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\), use a prespecified deterministic order only to implement a tie, and evaluate \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)/\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\).
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.
defs.def:ikmw-normalized-design-value:
For each regular design \(d\), define the source scores on the Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang normalization by
\[
 \psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{E,1})\phi_{E,d},
 \qquad
 \psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{O,1})\phi_{O,d},
\]
and define their source-conditional second moments by
\[
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=E]
 =(1-p_{E,1})^2V_{E,d},
\]
\[
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=O]
 =(1-p_{O,1})^2V_{O,d}.
\]
The profiled IKM-normalized value, its optimizer set, and the best-tie predictive approximation ratio are
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
 =\left(
 \sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 +\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \right)^2,
\]
\[
 D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
 =\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d',\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}.
\]
These objects are defined only as normalization-specific score moments and profiles. Their interpretation as causal efficiency bounds is supplied design by design by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\) after its causal-identification and regularity premises have been verified.

assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-outcomes: \((Y(a),S_{3d}(a))\perp S_{1d}(a)\mid S_{2d}(a),U,X,G=O\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:late-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{3d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:early-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{1d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

snapshot.stmt:
For the full-catalogue pilot selector, \(0\le\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)-\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\le2\varepsilon_m\) deterministically, and \(\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\subseteq\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\). Thus \(P\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\le P\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\to0\), with the right-hand event empty when every design is optimal. Under \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\), and \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), \(\varepsilon_m=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat\alpha_{d,m}-\alpha_d^*(P)|=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m)\), and uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\), after assigning the entire floor-count brace the value zero whenever either floor count is zero,
\[
B\left\{\frac{V_{E,d}}{\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor}+\frac{V_{O,d}}{\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor}\right\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m+B^{-1})=o_P(1).
\]
The deterministic tie rule selects one empirical minimizer, while consistency means membership in the full population optimizer set \(D^*(P)\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.

snapshot.stmt:
Fix an arbitrary \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) and write \(\theta_d(P)=\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}\). Conditional on the independent full-catalogue pilot, suppose that the purchased experimental and observational samples are mutually independent and consist of independent and identically distributed observations from \(P(\cdot\mid G=E)\) and \(P(\cdot\mid G=O)\), respectively.

Use a fixed integer \(L\ge2\) of observational-only cross-fitting folds. For deterministic \(d_B\in\mathcal D\) and \(\alpha_B\in(0,1)\), put
\[
 e_B=\left\lfloor\frac{\alpha_BB}{c_{E,d_B}}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad
 o_B=\left\lfloor\frac{(1-\alpha_B)B}{c_{O,d_B}}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad n_B=e_B+o_B,
\]
and let \(P_{B,d_B,\alpha_B}^{\circ}\) have source probabilities \(e_B/n_B\) and \(o_B/n_B\) and source-conditional laws \(P(\cdot\mid G=E)\) and \(P(\cdot\mid G=O)\). Write \(\|\cdot\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=\|\cdot\|_{L_2(P_{B,d_B,\alpha_B}^{\circ})}\). Along every deterministic sequence satisfying
\[
 |\alpha_B-\alpha_{d_B}^*(P)|\longrightarrow0, \tag{1}
\]
suppose, uniformly over \(1\le\ell\le L\), that with \(\Delta h_{B,\ell}=\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_{d_B}\) and \(\Delta q_{B,\ell}=\widehat q_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_{d_B}\),
\[
 \|T_{d_B}\Delta h_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\delta_{h,B}),
 \qquad
 \|\Delta h_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\rho_{h,B}), \tag{2}
\]
\[
 \|T_{d_B}^{\star}\Delta q_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\delta_{q,B}),
 \qquad
 \|\Delta q_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\rho_{q,B}), \tag{3}
\]
where all four deterministic rates are \(o(1)\) and
\[
 \min\{\delta_{h,B}\rho_{q,B},\rho_{h,B}\delta_{q,B}\}=o(B^{-1/2}). \tag{4}
\]
Suppose also that the foldwise empirical multipliers obey
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \max_{1\le\ell\le L}\bigl(&
 \|\mathbf 1\{G=O\}\Delta q_{B,\ell}(Y-h_{d_B})\|_{2,B}^{\circ}
 +\|\mathbf 1\{G=O\}q_{d_B}\Delta h_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}\\
 &+\|\mathbf 1\{G=O\}\Delta q_{B,\ell}\Delta h_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}
 \bigr)=o_P(1),
\end{aligned} \tag{5}
\]
with every bridge evaluated at its design-specific arguments. For each \(o_B\), partition the observational indices deterministically into balanced folds \(O_{B,1},\ldots,O_{B,L}\). Train \(\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}\) on \(O_B\setminus O_{B,\ell}\) and \(\widehat q_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}\) on \(E_B\cup(O_B\setminus O_{B,\ell})\), with any auxiliary training randomness independent of evaluation observations; assign every degenerate fit a fixed measurable value. Evaluate every experimental observation with every one of the \(L\) outcome-bridge fits.

For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), put
\[
 e_{B,a}=\sum_{i\in E_B}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\},
 \qquad
 o_{B,\ell,a}=\sum_{i\in O_{B,\ell}}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\},
\]
and, on positive denominators, define
\[
 \widehat p_{E,a}=e_{B,a}/e_B,
 \qquad
 \widehat p_{O,\ell,a}=o_{B,\ell,a}/|O_{B,\ell}|,
\]
\[
 \widehat\mu_{d_B,a}^{(-\ell)}
 =\frac1{e_{B,a}}\sum_{i\in E_B}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}
 \widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d_B,i},S_{2d_B,i},a,X_i),
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\mu_{B,d_B}(a)
 &=\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\widehat\mu_{d_B,a}^{(-\ell)}\\
 &\quad+\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\frac1{o_{B,\ell,a}}
 \sum_{i\in O_{B,\ell}}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}
 \widehat q_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{2d_B,i},S_{1d_B,i},a,X_i)\\
 &\hspace{36mm}\times
 \{Y_i-\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d_B,i},S_{2d_B,i},a,X_i)\},
\end{aligned} \tag{6}
\]
and \(\widehat\tau_B(d_B,\alpha_B)=\widehat\mu_{B,d_B}(1)-\widehat\mu_{B,d_B}(0)\). Define the exact arm-normalized plug-in scores by
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\phi_{E,d_B,B,i}
 =\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{a=0}^1(-1)^{1-a}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}}{\widehat p_{E,a}}
 \{&\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d_B,i},S_{2d_B,i},a,X_i)
 -\widehat\mu_{d_B,a}^{(-\ell)}\},
\end{aligned} \tag{7}
\]
for \(i\in E_B\), and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\phi_{O,d_B,B,i}
 &=\sum_{a=0}^1(-1)^{1-a}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}}{\widehat p_{O,\ell,a}}
 \widehat q_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{2d_B,i},S_{1d_B,i},a,X_i)\\
 &\hspace{22mm}\times
 \{Y_i-\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d_B,i},S_{2d_B,i},a,X_i)\},
 \qquad i\in O_{B,\ell}.
\end{aligned} \tag{8}
\]
Set \(\widetilde V_{E,d_B,B}=e_B^{-1}\sum_{i\in E_B}\widehat\phi_{E,d_B,B,i}^2\) and \(\widetilde V_{O,d_B,B}=o_B^{-1}\sum_{i\in O_B}\widehat\phi_{O,d_B,B,i}^2\). Every quantity in (6)--(8), including the two variance estimators, is assigned zero whenever one of its displayed denominators is zero.

Let \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\), assume \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), and assume that \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main study. Suppose
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,
 |\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m}),
 \qquad r_{V,m}=o(1), \tag{9}
\]
and
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}
 |\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B}),
 \qquad r_{\widetilde V,B}=o(1). \tag{10}
\]
Implement (6)--(8) at \((\widehat d_m,\widehat\alpha_m)\), and define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathsf D_B
 ={}&\{N_{E,B}\ge1,N_{O,B}\ge1\}
 \cap\bigcap_{a=0}^1\{e_{B,a}\ge1\}\\
 &{}\cap\bigcap_{\ell=1}^L\bigcap_{a=0}^1\{o_{B,\ell,a}\ge1\}.
\end{aligned} \tag{11}
\]
With all zero-denominator fractions assigned zero, set
\[
 \widehat s_B^2
 =\mathbf 1\{\mathsf D_B\}B\left\{
 \frac{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}}{N_{E,B}}
 +\frac{\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}}{N_{O,B}}
 \right\},
 \qquad
 \widehat s_B=(\widehat s_B^2)^{1/2}, \tag{12}
\]
and \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}=\mathsf D_B\cap\{\widehat s_B^2>0\}\). Let \(s_{0,B}\) be the nonnegative square root of
\[
 s_{0,B}^2
 =B\left\{\frac{V_{E,\widehat d_m}}{N_{E,B}}
 +\frac{V_{O,\widehat d_m}}{N_{O,B}}\right\} \tag{13}
\]
when both source counts are positive, and set \(s_{0,B}=0\) otherwise. On \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}\), set \(\widehat\tau_B=\widehat\tau_B(\widehat d_m,\widehat\alpha_m)\), define
\[
 \mathsf T_B=\frac{\sqrt B\{\widehat\tau_B-\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\}}{\widehat s_B},
 \qquad
 I_B=\left[\widehat\tau_B-z_{1-\eta/2}\frac{\widehat s_B}{\sqrt B},
 \widehat\tau_B+z_{1-\eta/2}\frac{\widehat s_B}{\sqrt B}\right], \tag{14}
\]
and on \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}^c\) set \(\widehat\tau_B=0\), \(\widehat s_B=0\), \(\mathsf T_B=0\), and \(I_B=[0,0]\). Then
\[
 P(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}})\longrightarrow1, \tag{15}
\]
\[
 s_{0,B}^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1),
 \qquad
 \widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1), \tag{16}
\]
\[
 \mathsf T_B\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1),
 \qquad
 P\{\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\in I_B\}\longrightarrow1-\eta. \tag{17}
\]
If, in addition, \(\theta_d(P)=\tau\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\), then \(\mathsf T_B\) is the same statistic centered at \(\tau\), \(\sqrt B(\widehat\tau_B-\tau)/\widehat s_B\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\) with the stipulated zero extension, and \(P\{\tau\in I_B\}\to1-\eta\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.
defs.def:selected-wald-variance:
Let \(\mathcal I_{E,B}\) and \(\mathcal I_{O,B}\) be the experimental and observational main-study index sets, of sizes \(N_{E,B}\) and \(N_{O,B}\). Use a fixed integer \(L\ge2\) and a deterministic balanced observational-only partition \(\mathcal I_{O,B}=\bigsqcup_{\ell=1}^L\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}\). For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), train \(\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}\) on \(\mathcal I_{O,B}\setminus\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}\), and train \(\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}\) on \(\mathcal I_{E,B}\cup(\mathcal I_{O,B}\setminus\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell})\). Assign any degenerate fit a fixed measurable value.

For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), define
\[
 e_{B,a}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{E,B}}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\},
 \qquad
 o_{B,\ell,a}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\},
\]
\[
 \widehat p_{E,a}=e_{B,a}/N_{E,B},
 \qquad
 \widehat p_{O,\ell,a}=o_{B,\ell,a}/|\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}|,
\]
and
\[
 \widehat\mu_{d,a}^{(-\ell)}
 =\frac1{e_{B,a}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{E,B}}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}
 \widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d,i},S_{2d,i},a,X_i).
\]
Every displayed quantity is assigned zero if one of its displayed denominators is zero. Whenever the required denominators are positive, set
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\mu_{B,d}(a)
 &=\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\widehat\mu_{d,a}^{(-\ell)}\\
 &\quad+\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\frac1{o_{B,\ell,a}}
 \sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}
 \widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{2d,i},S_{1d,i},a,X_i)\\
 &\hspace{35mm}\times
 \{Y_i-\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d,i},S_{2d,i},a,X_i)\},
\end{aligned}
\]
and \(\widehat\tau_B(d,\alpha)=\widehat\mu_{B,d}(1)-\widehat\mu_{B,d}(0)\). For \(i\in\mathcal I_{E,B}\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\phi_{E,d,B,i}
 =\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{a=0}^1(-1)^{1-a}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}}{\widehat p_{E,a}}
 \{&\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d,i},S_{2d,i},a,X_i)
 -\widehat\mu_{d,a}^{(-\ell)}\},
\end{aligned}
\]
and, for \(i\in\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\phi_{O,d,B,i}
 &=\sum_{a=0}^1(-1)^{1-a}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}}{\widehat p_{O,\ell,a}}
 \widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{2d,i},S_{1d,i},a,X_i)\\
 &\hspace{22mm}\times
 \{Y_i-\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d,i},S_{2d,i},a,X_i)\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every summand with a zero empirical arm probability is zero. Set
\[
 \widetilde V_{E,d,B}=N_{E,B}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{E,B}}\widehat\phi_{E,d,B,i}^2,
 \qquad
 \widetilde V_{O,d,B}=N_{O,B}^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{O,B,\ell}}\widehat\phi_{O,d,B,i}^2,
\]
with value zero when the corresponding source count is zero. At \((d,\alpha)=(\widehat d_m,\widehat\alpha_m)\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathsf D_B
 ={}&\{N_{E,B}\ge1,N_{O,B}\ge1\}
 \cap\bigcap_{a=0}^1\{e_{B,a}\ge1\}\\
 &{}\cap\bigcap_{\ell=1}^L\bigcap_{a=0}^1\{o_{B,\ell,a}\ge1\},
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
 \widehat s_B^2=\mathbf 1\{\mathsf D_B\}B\left\{
 \frac{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}}{N_{E,B}}
 +\frac{\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}}{N_{O,B}}\right\},
 \qquad
 \widehat s_B=(\widehat s_B^2)^{1/2},
\]
and \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}=\mathsf D_B\cap\{\widehat s_B^2>0\}\). Let \(s_{0,B}\) be the nonnegative square root of \(B\{V_{E,\widehat d_m}/N_{E,B}+V_{O,\widehat d_m}/N_{O,B}\}\) on positive source counts and zero otherwise. On \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}\), set \(\widehat\tau_B=\widehat\tau_B(\widehat d_m,\widehat\alpha_m)\), \(\mathsf T_B=\sqrt B\{\widehat\tau_B-\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\}/\widehat s_B\), and
\[
 I_B=\left[\widehat\tau_B-z_{1-\eta/2}\widehat s_B/\sqrt B,
 \widehat\tau_B+z_{1-\eta/2}\widehat s_B/\sqrt B\right].
\]
On \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}^c\), set \(\widehat\tau_B=0\), \(\widehat s_B=0\), \(\mathsf T_B=0\), and \(I_B=[0,0]\). Under common identification, \(\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)=\tau\), so the numerator of \(\mathsf T_B\) is equivalently \(\sqrt B(\widehat\tau_B-\tau)\). These conventions make every estimator, score moment, statistic, and interval a fixed measurable map on the entire sample space.

assumptions.ass:independent-pilot: \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main-study observations used to construct \(\widehat\tau_B\).
assumptions.ass:main-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.
assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).
assumptions.ass:uniform-outcome-strong-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{2,O,h,d}=O_P(\rho_{h,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.
assumptions.ass:uniform-outcome-weak-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat h_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_d\|_{w,h,d}=O_P(\delta_{h,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.
assumptions.ass:uniform-selection-strong-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{2,O,q,d}=O_P(\rho_{q,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.
assumptions.ass:uniform-selection-weak-rate: For fixed \(L\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat q_{d,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_d\|_{w,q,d}=O_P(\delta_{q,B})\), where probability is under the joint main-study law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and all folds.

For the full-catalogue pilot selector, \(0\le\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)-\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\le2\varepsilon_m\) deterministically, and \(\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\subseteq\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\). Thus \(P\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\le P\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}\to0\), with the right-hand event empty when every design is optimal. Under \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\), and \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), \(\varepsilon_m=O_P(r_{V,m})\), \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat\alpha_{d,m}-\alpha_d^*(P)|=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m)\), and uniformly over \(d\in\mathcal D\), after assigning the entire floor-count brace the value zero whenever either floor count is zero,
\[
B\left\{\frac{V_{E,d}}{\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor}+\frac{V_{O,d}}{\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor}\right\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)=O_P(r_{V,m}+\underline v_m+B^{-1})=o_P(1).
\]
The deterministic tie rule selects one empirical minimizer, while consistency means membership in the full population optimizer set \(D^*(P)\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile: For \(d\in\mathcal D\), set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}/\alpha+c_{O,d}V_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\) when the design is regular and set \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=+\infty\) otherwise.

assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.

snapshot.stmt:
Fix an arbitrary \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) and write \(\theta_d(P)=\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}\). Conditional on the independent full-catalogue pilot, suppose that the purchased experimental and observational samples are mutually independent and consist of independent and identically distributed observations from \(P(\cdot\mid G=E)\) and \(P(\cdot\mid G=O)\), respectively.

Use a fixed integer \(L\ge2\) of observational-only cross-fitting folds. For deterministic \(d_B\in\mathcal D\) and \(\alpha_B\in(0,1)\), put
\[
 e_B=\left\lfloor\frac{\alpha_BB}{c_{E,d_B}}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad
 o_B=\left\lfloor\frac{(1-\alpha_B)B}{c_{O,d_B}}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad n_B=e_B+o_B,
\]
and let \(P_{B,d_B,\alpha_B}^{\circ}\) have source probabilities \(e_B/n_B\) and \(o_B/n_B\) and source-conditional laws \(P(\cdot\mid G=E)\) and \(P(\cdot\mid G=O)\). Write \(\|\cdot\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=\|\cdot\|_{L_2(P_{B,d_B,\alpha_B}^{\circ})}\). Along every deterministic sequence satisfying
\[
 |\alpha_B-\alpha_{d_B}^*(P)|\longrightarrow0, \tag{1}
\]
suppose, uniformly over \(1\le\ell\le L\), that with \(\Delta h_{B,\ell}=\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_{d_B}\) and \(\Delta q_{B,\ell}=\widehat q_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_{d_B}\),
\[
 \|T_{d_B}\Delta h_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\delta_{h,B}),
 \qquad
 \|\Delta h_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\rho_{h,B}), \tag{2}
\]
\[
 \|T_{d_B}^{\star}\Delta q_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\delta_{q,B}),
 \qquad
 \|\Delta q_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\rho_{q,B}), \tag{3}
\]
where all four deterministic rates are \(o(1)\) and
\[
 \min\{\delta_{h,B}\rho_{q,B},\rho_{h,B}\delta_{q,B}\}=o(B^{-1/2}). \tag{4}
\]
Suppose also that the foldwise empirical multipliers obey
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \max_{1\le\ell\le L}\bigl(&
 \|\mathbf 1\{G=O\}\Delta q_{B,\ell}(Y-h_{d_B})\|_{2,B}^{\circ}
 +\|\mathbf 1\{G=O\}q_{d_B}\Delta h_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}\\
 &+\|\mathbf 1\{G=O\}\Delta q_{B,\ell}\Delta h_{B,\ell}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}
 \bigr)=o_P(1),
\end{aligned} \tag{5}
\]
with every bridge evaluated at its design-specific arguments. For each \(o_B\), partition the observational indices deterministically into balanced folds \(O_{B,1},\ldots,O_{B,L}\). Train \(\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}\) on \(O_B\setminus O_{B,\ell}\) and \(\widehat q_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}\) on \(E_B\cup(O_B\setminus O_{B,\ell})\), with any auxiliary training randomness independent of evaluation observations; assign every degenerate fit a fixed measurable value. Evaluate every experimental observation with every one of the \(L\) outcome-bridge fits.

For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), put
\[
 e_{B,a}=\sum_{i\in E_B}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\},
 \qquad
 o_{B,\ell,a}=\sum_{i\in O_{B,\ell}}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\},
\]
and, on positive denominators, define
\[
 \widehat p_{E,a}=e_{B,a}/e_B,
 \qquad
 \widehat p_{O,\ell,a}=o_{B,\ell,a}/|O_{B,\ell}|,
\]
\[
 \widehat\mu_{d_B,a}^{(-\ell)}
 =\frac1{e_{B,a}}\sum_{i\in E_B}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}
 \widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d_B,i},S_{2d_B,i},a,X_i),
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\mu_{B,d_B}(a)
 &=\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\widehat\mu_{d_B,a}^{(-\ell)}\\
 &\quad+\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\frac1{o_{B,\ell,a}}
 \sum_{i\in O_{B,\ell}}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}
 \widehat q_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{2d_B,i},S_{1d_B,i},a,X_i)\\
 &\hspace{36mm}\times
 \{Y_i-\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d_B,i},S_{2d_B,i},a,X_i)\},
\end{aligned} \tag{6}
\]
and \(\widehat\tau_B(d_B,\alpha_B)=\widehat\mu_{B,d_B}(1)-\widehat\mu_{B,d_B}(0)\). Define the exact arm-normalized plug-in scores by
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\phi_{E,d_B,B,i}
 =\frac1L\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{a=0}^1(-1)^{1-a}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}}{\widehat p_{E,a}}
 \{&\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d_B,i},S_{2d_B,i},a,X_i)
 -\widehat\mu_{d_B,a}^{(-\ell)}\},
\end{aligned} \tag{7}
\]
for \(i\in E_B\), and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\phi_{O,d_B,B,i}
 &=\sum_{a=0}^1(-1)^{1-a}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}}{\widehat p_{O,\ell,a}}
 \widehat q_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{2d_B,i},S_{1d_B,i},a,X_i)\\
 &\hspace{22mm}\times
 \{Y_i-\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}(S_{3d_B,i},S_{2d_B,i},a,X_i)\},
 \qquad i\in O_{B,\ell}.
\end{aligned} \tag{8}
\]
Set \(\widetilde V_{E,d_B,B}=e_B^{-1}\sum_{i\in E_B}\widehat\phi_{E,d_B,B,i}^2\) and \(\widetilde V_{O,d_B,B}=o_B^{-1}\sum_{i\in O_B}\widehat\phi_{O,d_B,B,i}^2\). Every quantity in (6)--(8), including the two variance estimators, is assigned zero whenever one of its displayed denominators is zero.

Let \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\), assume \(\underline v_m=o(1)\), and assume that \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main study. Suppose
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,
 |\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m}),
 \qquad r_{V,m}=o(1), \tag{9}
\]
and
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D,\,g\in\{E,O\}}
 |\widetilde V_{g,d,B}-V_{g,d}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B}),
 \qquad r_{\widetilde V,B}=o(1). \tag{10}
\]
Implement (6)--(8) at \((\widehat d_m,\widehat\alpha_m)\), and define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathsf D_B
 ={}&\{N_{E,B}\ge1,N_{O,B}\ge1\}
 \cap\bigcap_{a=0}^1\{e_{B,a}\ge1\}\\
 &{}\cap\bigcap_{\ell=1}^L\bigcap_{a=0}^1\{o_{B,\ell,a}\ge1\}.
\end{aligned} \tag{11}
\]
With all zero-denominator fractions assigned zero, set
\[
 \widehat s_B^2
 =\mathbf 1\{\mathsf D_B\}B\left\{
 \frac{\widetilde V_{E,\widehat d_m,B}}{N_{E,B}}
 +\frac{\widetilde V_{O,\widehat d_m,B}}{N_{O,B}}
 \right\},
 \qquad
 \widehat s_B=(\widehat s_B^2)^{1/2}, \tag{12}
\]
and \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}=\mathsf D_B\cap\{\widehat s_B^2>0\}\). Let \(s_{0,B}\) be the nonnegative square root of
\[
 s_{0,B}^2
 =B\left\{\frac{V_{E,\widehat d_m}}{N_{E,B}}
 +\frac{V_{O,\widehat d_m}}{N_{O,B}}\right\} \tag{13}
\]
when both source counts are positive, and set \(s_{0,B}=0\) otherwise. On \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}\), set \(\widehat\tau_B=\widehat\tau_B(\widehat d_m,\widehat\alpha_m)\), define
\[
 \mathsf T_B=\frac{\sqrt B\{\widehat\tau_B-\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\}}{\widehat s_B},
 \qquad
 I_B=\left[\widehat\tau_B-z_{1-\eta/2}\frac{\widehat s_B}{\sqrt B},
 \widehat\tau_B+z_{1-\eta/2}\frac{\widehat s_B}{\sqrt B}\right], \tag{14}
\]
and on \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}^c\) set \(\widehat\tau_B=0\), \(\widehat s_B=0\), \(\mathsf T_B=0\), and \(I_B=[0,0]\). Then
\[
 P(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}})\longrightarrow1, \tag{15}
\]
\[
 s_{0,B}^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1),
 \qquad
 \widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1), \tag{16}
\]
\[
 \mathsf T_B\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1),
 \qquad
 P\{\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\in I_B\}\longrightarrow1-\eta. \tag{17}
\]
If, in addition, \(\theta_d(P)=\tau\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\), then \(\mathsf T_B\) is the same statistic centered at \(\tau\), \(\sqrt B(\widehat\tau_B-\tau)/\widehat s_B\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\) with the stipulated zero extension, and \(P\{\tau\in I_B\}\to1-\eta\).
