=\mathbb E_P[h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O].
\]
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

snapshot.stmt:
Fix any prescribed \(\chi>1\). Under the IKM score and profile normalization, every binary center law satisfies, for \(d\in\mathcal D\),
\[
 \psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac12\phi_{E,d},
 \qquad
 \psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac12\phi_{O,d},
 \qquad
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},
\]
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon).
\]
Consequently \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon)=\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)\). For each fixed \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), there is \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}>0\) such that every law \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\) with \(\|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) is regular, both admissible bridge contrasts equal \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 >\frac12\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon).
\]
On this neighborhood, the IKM-normalized profile is the profiled local causal semiparametric efficiency bound under the fixed-system conditions in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\).

defs.def:binary-witness:
Fix an arbitrary prescribed \(\chi>1\). Set \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=(5\chi-3)/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=(5\chi-3)/2\), and put
\[
 y_{\chi}=\sqrt{1-\frac{3}{10\chi}}.
\]
Let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form
\[
 Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}),
\]
while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{y_{\chi}}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then
\[
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi-1}{2},\qquad
 c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi+1}{2},\qquad
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2,\qquad c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3,
\]
so the paired costs are \(5\chi\) and \(5\), respectively. For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are
\[
 h_d(l,a)=\frac{l}{y},
 \qquad
 q_d(e,a)=\frac{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)}{1-1/16},
\]
and the residual prediction variance is
\[
 R(x,y)=\frac{(1-x^2)(1-y^2)}{1-x^2y^2}.
\]

The \emph{binary constrained finite-cell model} \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\) is the family of laws \(P\) with the preceding prescribed catalogue, costs, cap, and role assignments, constant \(X\) and constant \(S_{2d}\), latent variables \(U,T,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4\in\{-1,1\}\), \(A=(T+1)/2\), and potential variables
\[
 Z(a)=(W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4),\qquad Y(a)=U,
 \qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For strictly positive probability vectors \((\pi_g:g\in\{E,O\})\), \((\nu_u:u\in\{-1,1\})\), \((\lambda_t:t\in\{-1,1\})\), observational treatment kernels \(e_u(t)\), and proxy kernels \(k_{j,u}(w)\), its latent-cell mass factorizes as
\[
 P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
 =\pi_g\nu_u\bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t
 +\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}
 \prod_{j=1}^4k_{j,u}(w_j). \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(U\) is independent of \(G\), treatment is randomized independently of \(U\) in source \(E\), and the four proxies are mutually independent conditional on \(U\) and invariant across source and treatment. The design \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \((W_1,W_2)\) to roles one and three, and \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \((W_3,W_4)\) to roles one and three; role two is constant. For each \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), the preceding center \(P_\epsilon\) is the point having \(\pi_E=\pi_O=1/2\), \(\nu_{-1}=\nu_1=1/2\), \(\lambda_{-1}=\lambda_1=1/2\), \(e_u(t)=(1+tu/4)/2\), and
\[
 k_{j,u}(w)=\frac{1+s_juw}{2},
 \qquad
 (s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4)=(\epsilon,y_{\chi},1/2,1/2).
\]
The model is parameterized by the relative interiors of these finite probability simplices. Its relative topology is equivalently the Euclidean parameter topology or the maximum-norm topology \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{cell}}\) induced by the complete latent-cell vector in (1).
defs.def:regular-law-class: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) is the subclass of \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) satisfying long- and short-term consistency, observational latent exchangeability and overlap, experimental randomization and overlap, full short-term external validity, source support, the sequential-outcome restriction, and both proxy-completeness conditions for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
defs.def:predictive-benchmark:
For each \(d\in\mathcal D\), compute the observational residual prediction risk
\[
R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O]
\]
and define the newly introduced paired-source diagnostic
\[
\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=\frac{(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)}{B}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\) retain every minimizer of this diagnostic, and define
\[
\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=
\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
{\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
The notation records that the diagnostic is shaped by a residual-risk-per-budget calculation; it is not attributed as a proxy-selection workflow or guarantee of Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile:
For \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and \(0<\alpha<1\), set
\[
\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=\frac{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}{\alpha}+\frac{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}{1-\alpha}.
\]
Set the value to \(+\infty\) outside the observable regular set.
defs.def:common-identification-class:
\[
\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}
=\{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}:\theta_d(P)=\tau\text{ for every }d\in\mathcal D\}.
\]
defs.def:ikmw-normalized-design-value:
For each regular design \(d\), define the source scores on the Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang normalization by
\[
 \psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{E,1})\phi_{E,d},
 \qquad
 \psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{O,1})\phi_{O,d},
\]
and define their source-conditional second moments by
\[
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=E]
 =(1-p_{E,1})^2V_{E,d},
\]
\[
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=O]
 =(1-p_{O,1})^2V_{O,d}.
\]
The profiled IKM-normalized value, its optimizer set, and the best-tie paired-source diagnostic approximation ratio are
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
 =\left(
 \sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 +\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \right)^2,
\]
\[
 D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
 =\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d',\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}.
\]
These objects are defined only as normalization-specific score moments and profiles. Their interpretation as causal efficiency bounds is supplied design by design by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\) after its causal-identification and regularity premises have been verified.

assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).

assumptions.ass:late-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{3d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(B>0\), and abbreviate
\[
 p_d=\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B),
 \qquad
 v_d=\mathcal V_d^*(P).
\]
Define the prediction-order relation and its order-restricted design-value constant by
\[
 \mathcal O_P
 =\{(d,d')\in\mathcal D^2:p_d\le p_{d'}\},
 \qquad
 C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)
 =\max_{(d,d')\in\mathcal O_P}\frac{v_d}{v_{d'}}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Then \(1\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty\), and, for every \(C\ge0\),
\[
 \bigl[p_d\le p_{d'}\Longrightarrow v_d\le C v_{d'}
 \text{ for all }d,d'\in\mathcal D\bigr]
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 C\ge C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P).
 \tag{2}
\]
The smallest constant for the actual best-tie paired-source diagnostic rule is instead
\[
 C_{\mathrm{sel}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}v_d}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}v_{d'}}
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P),
 \qquad
 1\le C_{\mathrm{sel}}(P)\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty.
 \tag{3}
\]
Consequently, for any nonempty subclass \(\mathcal Q\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), a finite constant uniform over \(\mathcal Q\) exists for the best-tie rule if and only if
\(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)<\infty\); for all pairwise prediction-order implications it exists if and only if
\(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty\).  Thus (1), rather than an operator norm, is the weakest exact lawwise comparison for selection by this newly defined diagnostic.  The design-specific operators \(T_d\) enter (1) through the bridges and hence through \(v_d\), but no further comparison of the operators is necessary for lawwise finiteness.

More specifically, consider any numerical realization of the handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{comp}}\) with the following properties.  For each \(d\), it supplies a real vector space \(\mathcal H_d\), a cone \(\mathcal X_d(P)\subseteq\mathcal H_d\setminus\{0\}\) containing a transported law-specific direction \(x_d(P)\), a positive prediction quadratic form \(Q_{R,d}\) on that cone, and two nonnegative source-score quadratic forms \(Q_{E,d}\) and \(Q_{O,d}\), with
\[
 Bp_d=Q_{R,d}\{x_d(P)\},
 \qquad
 v_d=F_d\{x_d(P)\},
 \tag{4}
\]
where
\[
 F_d(x)
 =\left\{
 \sqrt{c_{E,d}Q_{E,d}(x)}
 +\sqrt{c_{O,d}Q_{O,d}(x)}
 \right\}^2.
 \tag{5}
\]
On the bridge-differentiable submodel class of Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}bridge\text{-}differentiable\text{-}submodel}\), these source scores are gradient components; outside that class, only the source-score interpretation is asserted.  Set
\[
 \Lambda_-(P)
 =\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\inf_{x\in\mathcal X_d(P)}
 \frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}(x)},
 \qquad
 \Lambda_+(P)
 =\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X_d(P)}
 \frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}(x)}.
 \tag{6}
\]
The weakest two-sided quadratic-form envelope on the chosen cones is precisely
\[
 0<\Lambda_-(P)\le\Lambda_+(P)<\infty,
 \tag{7}
\]
and it implies the valid, generally conservative certificate
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 \le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)
 \le\frac{\Lambda_+(P)}{\Lambda_-(P)}.
 \tag{8}
\]

The sharp constant in (2) or (3) is not, in general, a largest generalized eigenvalue.  Indeed,
\[
 F_d(x)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}
 \left\{
 \frac{c_{E,d}Q_{E,d}(x)}{\alpha}
 +\frac{c_{O,d}Q_{O,d}(x)}{1-\alpha}
 \right\},
 \tag{9}
\]
so the profiled numerator is generally not a quadratic form.  If \(\mathcal H_d\) is finite dimensional, \(Q_{R,d}\) is positive definite, and \(\mathcal X_d(P)=\mathcal H_d\setminus\{0\}\), a largest generalized eigenvalue at a fixed \(\alpha\) gives only a one-sided full-space envelope.  Selection requires both the upper and lower envelopes in (6), and equality in (8) additionally requires saturation by law-realized, diagnostic-ordered directions.  Hence equality with a largest generalized eigenvalue can hold only after adding a common-space representation, a normalization of the positive lower envelope, and the required saturation; none follows from observable-law operator bijectivity or from the diagnostic ordering alone.

defs.def:bridge-differentiable-submodel:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(d\in\mathcal D\), and write
\[
 H_d=(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X),\qquad L_d=(S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X).
\]
A regular two-source parametric submodel \(\{P_t:|t|<t_0\}\) through \(P=P_0\), with source-conditional scores \(\ell_E\) and \(\ell_O\), is called \emph{bridge-differentiable for design \(d\) at \(P\)} when the following conditions hold.  First, the source-conditional laws are dominated on a common support and the path is differentiable in quadratic mean in each source.  Second, for all sufficiently small \(|t|\), \(P_t\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and its design-\(d\) outcome bridge \(h_{d,t}\) is unique.  Third, after identifying the common \(L_2\) coordinate spaces along the dominated path, there is \(\dot h_d\in L_2(H_d\mid G=O)\) such that
\[
 \left\|\frac{h_{d,t}-h_{d,0}}{t}-\dot h_d\right\|_{L_2(P(\cdot\mid G=O))}\longrightarrow0,
\]
and the conditional bridge equation
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_t}\{Y-h_{d,t}(H_d)\mid L_d,G=O\}=0
\]
may be differentiated at \(t=0\) in \(L_2(L_d\mid G=O)\) using the conditional-score rule.  This is a restriction on submodels, not a consequence of pointwise bijectivity of \(T_d\).
defs.def:operator-comparison-handle: Use \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{comp}}\) to compare the source-score quadratic forms underlying \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)\) with the residual-risk quadratic form underlying the newly defined paired-source diagnostic \(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\).  These source-score forms have a gradient interpretation only along the bridge-differentiable paths declared for design \(d\).  The exact target is a lawwise constant bounding \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\); the handle does not assert that a generalized eigenvalue is sharp, does not give an unconditional gradient or causal-efficiency interpretation, and does not represent a published proxy-selection workflow.

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), the exact fixed-catalogue diagnostic identity is
\[
 1\le\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d'}V_{E,d'}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d'}V_{O,d'}})^2}<\infty.
\]
The smallest constant in the actual best-tie inequality is exactly \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\). The least constant that makes every pairwise implication
\(\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)\Rightarrow \mathcal V_d^*(P)\le C(P)\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\)
valid is
\[
 \max_{\substack{d,d'\in\mathcal D:\,
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\le\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d'}(P;B)}}
 \frac{\mathcal V_d^*(P)}{\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
Every displayed constant is finite at a fixed \(P\). Nevertheless, for every prescribed finite \(\chi>1\), the \(\chi\)-indexed binary region satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\), even though the uniquely diagnostic-selected design has paired cost \(\chi\) times that of the arm-normalized source-score-optimal design at the center laws. Across all center cost-disadvantage factors, every minimizing sequence satisfies
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)
 \sim\frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15}\epsilon^{-2/3},
\]
and the exact least-divergent envelope obeys
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 &=\epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\\
 &=\frac1{726}+\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}\epsilon^{2/3}
 +o(\epsilon^{2/3}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) yields an exact law-specific enumeration, not a primitive uniform diagnostic-to-source-score guarantee; optimizing the witness's cost disadvantage does not remove the leading \(1/(726\epsilon^2)\) divergence.

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.

For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and fixed \(0<\alpha<1\), as \(B\to\infty\),
\[
B\left\{\frac{V_{E,d}}{n_{E,B}(d,\alpha)}+\frac{V_{O,d}}{n_{O,B}(d,\alpha)}\right\}
=\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)+\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P),
\]
where, once \(B\ge2\max\{c_{E,d}/\alpha,c_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\}\),
\[
0\le\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)\le \frac2B\left\{
\frac{V_{E,d}c_{E,d}^2}{\alpha^2}+
\frac{V_{O,d}c_{O,d}^2}{(1-\alpha)^2}\right\}.
\]
Thus the floor-count source-score variance converges to \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\). The unique minimizer and minimum are
\[
\alpha_d^*(P)=\frac{\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}}{\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}},
\qquad
\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\left(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}\right)^2.
\]
On the bridge-differentiable submodel class of Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}bridge\text{-}differentiable\text{-}submodel}\), this profiles the designwise gradient variance. For \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}\), it profiles the gradient variance of the common causal target only on that declared submodel class. It is a local causal semiparametric efficiency bound only when the designwise gradient is additionally canonical for \(\tau\), in particular under the fixed-system Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang conditions recorded separately.

Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\). Conditional on the independent full-catalogue pilot, suppose the purchased experimental and observational samples are mutually independent and independent and identically distributed within source. Use the selected-design-only estimator, score moments, total event, variance estimator, statistic, and interval of Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}selected\text{-}wald\text{-}variance}\). Impose the maintained estimator-level conditions in Assumptions~\(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}outcome\text{-}weak\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}outcome\text{-}strong\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}selection\text{-}weak\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}selection\text{-}strong\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}bridge\text{-}product\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}postselection\text{-}multiplier\text{-}condition}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}pilot\text{-}gradient\text{-}variance\text{-}rate}\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}main\text{-}gradient\text{-}variance\text{-}rate}\), together with the four declared bridge-rate vanishing conditions and the pilot and main-study variance-rate vanishing conditions. Let \(m\to\infty\), \(B\to\infty\), and \(\underline v_m=o(1)\). Then
\[
 P(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}})\longrightarrow1,
\]
\[
 s_{0,B}^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1),
 \qquad
 \widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1),
\]
and the selected observable contrast obeys
\[
 \mathsf T_B=
 \frac{\sqrt B\{\widehat\tau_B-\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\}}{\widehat s_B}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1),
 \qquad
 P\{\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\in I_B\}\longrightarrow1-\eta.
\]
All listed nuisance-rate, product-rate, multiplier, pilot-variance, and main-study-variance requirements are maintained sufficient conditions of this theorem. They are not conclusions of the observable law class or of the cited fixed-design theory, and concrete bridge learners and primitive conditions implying them remain the separate open object \(\mathrm{oeq{:}primitive\text{-}selected\text{-}path\text{-}attainability}\).

assumptions.ass:main-gradient-variance-rate:
Under the joint pilot and main-study law,
\[
 \max_{g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,\widehat d_m,B}-V_{g,\widehat d_m}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B}).
\]

=\mathbb E_P[h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O].

For every deterministic sequence \(d_B\in\mathcal D\), \(\alpha_B\in(0,1)\) with \(|\alpha_B-\alpha_{d_B}^*(P)|\to0\), and fixed \(L\),

\]

snapshot.stmt:
For the paper's newly defined paired-source residual-risk diagnostic, the following impossibility holds. For every prescribed finite cost-disadvantage factor \(\chi>1\), the generalized unequal-cost binary witness has paired costs \(5\chi\) for \(d_{\mathrm p}\) and \(5\) for \(d_{\mathrm e}\). For every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), the center law \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) is regular for both designs and both bridge contrasts equal \(\tau=0\). Nevertheless, \(d_{\mathrm p}\) is the unique minimizer of that diagnostic, while \(d_{\mathrm e}\) is the unique minimizer of both the arm-normalized source-score profile and the IKM-normalized local causal-efficiency profile. More precisely,
\[
 B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}(P_\epsilon;B)
 =\frac32\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2y_\chi^2}
 <\frac32<3
 =B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm e}}(P_\epsilon;B),
\]
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}+O_\chi(1),
 \qquad
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},
\]
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}
 +O_\chi(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
Across the center family, let \(\chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)\) be any cost-disadvantage factor minimizing the exact ratio for sufficiently small \(\epsilon\). Then
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)
 \sim \frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15}\epsilon^{-2/3},
\]
and the least-divergent sharp elbow is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 &=\epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\\
 &=\frac1{726}+\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}\epsilon^{2/3}
 +o(\epsilon^{2/3}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, both bridge contrasts equal \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty.
\]
On the relatively open subregion \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\subseteq\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\), every design remains regular and identifies \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)=\infty.
\]
For each prescribed \(\chi>1\), the center cost vector belongs to \(\mathcal C_\kappa\), has paired-cost ratio exactly \(\chi\), and has a relatively open neighborhood in \(\mathcal C_\kappa\) on which \(d_{\mathrm p}\) remains strictly more expensive and uniquely diagnostic-selected for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\), while both the arm-normalized and balanced-center IKM-normalized ratios diverge along the center-law path. Thus selection by this paper's paired-source residual-risk diagnostic has no finite uniform efficiency guarantee even when its chosen design is required to bear any prescribed finite cost disadvantage; even the least-divergent cost-disadvantage sequence grows at order \(\epsilon^{-2/3}\), and its ratio retains the leading divergence \(1/(726\epsilon^2)\). This result concerns only the newly defined diagnostic. It neither attributes a proxy-selection rule to a published paper nor refutes predictive proxy selection generally. The IKM-normalized profile has its absolute causal-efficiency interpretation only under the separately stated fixed-system premises; the arm-normalized profile is a source-score design value on the full regular class and a gradient design value only on bridge-differentiable submodels.

defs.def:binary-witness:
Fix an arbitrary prescribed \(\chi>1\). Set \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=(5\chi-3)/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=(5\chi-3)/2\), and put
\[
 y_{\chi}=\sqrt{1-\frac{3}{10\chi}}.
\]
Let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form
\[
 Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}),
\]
while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{y_{\chi}}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then
\[
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi-1}{2},\qquad
 c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi+1}{2},\qquad
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2,\qquad c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3,
\]
so the paired costs are \(5\chi\) and \(5\), respectively. For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are
\[
 h_d(l,a)=\frac{l}{y},
 \qquad
 q_d(e,a)=\frac{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)}{1-1/16},
\]
and the residual prediction variance is
\[
 R(x,y)=\frac{(1-x^2)(1-y^2)}{1-x^2y^2}.
\]

The \emph{binary constrained finite-cell model} \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\) is the family of laws \(P\) with the preceding prescribed catalogue, costs, cap, and role assignments, constant \(X\) and constant \(S_{2d}\), latent variables \(U,T,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4\in\{-1,1\}\), \(A=(T+1)/2\), and potential variables
\[
 Z(a)=(W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4),\qquad Y(a)=U,
 \qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For strictly positive probability vectors \((\pi_g:g\in\{E,O\})\), \((\nu_u:u\in\{-1,1\})\), \((\lambda_t:t\in\{-1,1\})\), observational treatment kernels \(e_u(t)\), and proxy kernels \(k_{j,u}(w)\), its latent-cell mass factorizes as
\[
 P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
 =\pi_g\nu_u\bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t
 +\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}
 \prod_{j=1}^4k_{j,u}(w_j). \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(U\) is independent of \(G\), treatment is randomized independently of \(U\) in source \(E\), and the four proxies are mutually independent conditional on \(U\) and invariant across source and treatment. The design \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \((W_1,W_2)\) to roles one and three, and \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \((W_3,W_4)\) to roles one and three; role two is constant. For each \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), the preceding center \(P_\epsilon\) is the point having \(\pi_E=\pi_O=1/2\), \(\nu_{-1}=\nu_1=1/2\), \(\lambda_{-1}=\lambda_1=1/2\), \(e_u(t)=(1+tu/4)/2\), and
\[
 k_{j,u}(w)=\frac{1+s_juw}{2},
 \qquad
 (s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4)=(\epsilon,y_{\chi},1/2,1/2).
\]
The model is parameterized by the relative interiors of these finite probability simplices. Its relative topology is equivalently the Euclidean parameter topology or the maximum-norm topology \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{cell}}\) induced by the complete latent-cell vector in (1).
defs.def:regular-law-class: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) is the subclass of \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) satisfying long- and short-term consistency, observational latent exchangeability and overlap, experimental randomization and overlap, full short-term external validity, source support, the sequential-outcome restriction, and both proxy-completeness conditions for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
defs.def:predictive-benchmark:
For each \(d\in\mathcal D\), compute the observational residual prediction risk
\[
R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O]
\]
and define the newly introduced paired-source diagnostic
\[
\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=\frac{(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)}{B}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\) retain every minimizer of this diagnostic, and define
\[
\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=
\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
{\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
The notation records that the diagnostic is shaped by a residual-risk-per-budget calculation; it is not attributed as a proxy-selection workflow or guarantee of Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile:
For \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and \(0<\alpha<1\), set
\[
\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=\frac{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}{\alpha}+\frac{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}{1-\alpha}.
\]
Set the value to \(+\infty\) outside the observable regular set.
defs.def:common-identification-class:
\[
\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}
=\{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}:\theta_d(P)=\tau\text{ for every }d\in\mathcal D\}.
\]
defs.def:ikmw-normalized-design-value:
For each regular design \(d\), define the source scores on the Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang normalization by
\[
 \psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{E,1})\phi_{E,d},
 \qquad
 \psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{O,1})\phi_{O,d},
\]
and define their source-conditional second moments by
\[
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=E]
 =(1-p_{E,1})^2V_{E,d},
\]
\[
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=O]
 =(1-p_{O,1})^2V_{O,d}.
\]
The profiled IKM-normalized value, its optimizer set, and the best-tie paired-source diagnostic approximation ratio are
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
 =\left(
 \sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 +\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \right)^2,
\]
\[
 D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
 =\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d',\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}.
\]
These objects are defined only as normalization-specific score moments and profiles. Their interpretation as causal efficiency bounds is supplied design by design by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\) after its causal-identification and regularity premises have been verified.

assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-outcomes: \((Y(a),S_{3d}(a))\perp S_{1d}(a)\mid S_{2d}(a),U,X,G=O\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:late-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{3d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:early-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{1d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:observed-outcome-bridge-existence:
For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(h_d\) is a square-integrable solution of
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O]
=\mathbb E_P[h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O].
\]
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile:
For \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and \(0<\alpha<1\), set
\[
\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=\frac{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}{\alpha}+\frac{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}{1-\alpha}.
\]
Set the value to \(+\infty\) outside the observable regular set.

assumptions.ass:observed-outcome-bridge-existence:
For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(h_d\) is a square-integrable solution of
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O]
=\mathbb E_P[h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O].
\]
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\). Conditional on the independent full-catalogue pilot, suppose the purchased experimental and observational samples are mutually independent and independent and identically distributed within source. Use the selected-design-only estimator, score moments, total event, variance estimator, statistic, and interval of Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}selected\text{-}wald\text{-}variance}\). Impose the maintained estimator-level conditions in Assumptions~\(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}outcome\text{-}weak\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}outcome\text{-}strong\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}selection\text{-}weak\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}selection\text{-}strong\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}bridge\text{-}product\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}postselection\text{-}multiplier\text{-}condition}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}pilot\text{-}gradient\text{-}variance\text{-}rate}\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}main\text{-}gradient\text{-}variance\text{-}rate}\), together with the four declared bridge-rate vanishing conditions and the pilot and main-study variance-rate vanishing conditions. Let \(m\to\infty\), \(B\to\infty\), and \(\underline v_m=o(1)\). Then
\[
 P(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}})\longrightarrow1,
\]
\[
 s_{0,B}^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1),
 \qquad
 \widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1),
\]
and the selected observable contrast obeys
\[
 \mathsf T_B=
 \frac{\sqrt B\{\widehat\tau_B-\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\}}{\widehat s_B}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1),
 \qquad
 P\{\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\in I_B\}\longrightarrow1-\eta.
\]
All listed nuisance-rate, product-rate, multiplier, pilot-variance, and main-study-variance requirements are maintained sufficient conditions of this theorem. They are not conclusions of the observable law class or of the cited fixed-design theory, and concrete bridge learners and primitive conditions implying them remain the separate open object \(\mathrm{oeq{:}primitive\text{-}selected\text{-}path\text{-}attainability}\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.

Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).

For \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and \(0<\alpha<1\), set
\[
\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=\frac{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}{\alpha}+\frac{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}{1-\alpha}.

Set the value to \(+\infty\) outside the observable regular set.

assumptions.ass:independent-pilot: \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main-study observations used to construct \(\widehat\tau_B\).
assumptions.ass:main-gradient-variance-rate:
Under the joint pilot and main-study law,
\[
 \max_{g\in\{E,O\}}|\widetilde V_{g,\widehat d_m,B}-V_{g,\widehat d_m}|=O_P(r_{\widetilde V,B}).
\]
assumptions.ass:observed-outcome-bridge-existence:
For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(h_d\) is a square-integrable solution of
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O]
=\mathbb E_P[h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O].
\]
assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).
assumptions.ass:uniform-outcome-strong-rate:
For every deterministic sequence \(d_B\in\mathcal D\), \(\alpha_B\in(0,1)\) with \(|\alpha_B-\alpha_{d_B}^*(P)|\to0\), and fixed \(L\),
\[
\max_{1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_{d_B}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\rho_{h,B}).
\]
assumptions.ass:uniform-outcome-weak-rate:
For every deterministic sequence \(d_B\in\mathcal D\), \(\alpha_B\in(0,1)\) with \(|\alpha_B-\alpha_{d_B}^*(P)|\to0\), and fixed \(L\),
\[
\max_{1\le\ell\le L}\|T_{d_B}(\widehat h_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}-h_{d_B})\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\delta_{h,B}).
\]
assumptions.ass:uniform-selection-strong-rate:
For every deterministic sequence \(d_B\in\mathcal D\), \(\alpha_B\in(0,1)\) with \(|\alpha_B-\alpha_{d_B}^*(P)|\to0\), and fixed \(L\),
\[
\max_{1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat q_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_{d_B}\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\rho_{q,B}).
\]
assumptions.ass:uniform-selection-weak-rate:
For every deterministic sequence \(d_B\in\mathcal D\), \(\alpha_B\in(0,1)\) with \(|\alpha_B-\alpha_{d_B}^*(P)|\to0\), and fixed \(L\),
\[
\max_{1\le\ell\le L}\|T_{d_B}^{\star}(\widehat q_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_{d_B})\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\delta_{q,B}).
\]

snapshot.stmt:
For the paper's newly defined paired-source residual-risk diagnostic, the following impossibility holds. For every prescribed finite cost-disadvantage factor \(\chi>1\), the generalized unequal-cost binary witness has paired costs \(5\chi\) for \(d_{\mathrm p}\) and \(5\) for \(d_{\mathrm e}\). For every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), the center law \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) is regular for both designs and both bridge contrasts equal \(\tau=0\). Nevertheless, \(d_{\mathrm p}\) is the unique minimizer of that diagnostic, while \(d_{\mathrm e}\) is the unique minimizer of both the arm-normalized source-score profile and the IKM-normalized local causal-efficiency profile. More precisely,
\[
 B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}(P_\epsilon;B)
 =\frac32\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2y_\chi^2}
 <\frac32<3
 =B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm e}}(P_\epsilon;B),
\]
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}+O_\chi(1),
 \qquad
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},
\]
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_\epsilon),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}
 +O_\chi(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
Across the center family, let \(\chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)\) be any cost-disadvantage factor minimizing the exact ratio for sufficiently small \(\epsilon\). Then
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)
 \sim \frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15}\epsilon^{-2/3},
\]
and the least-divergent sharp elbow is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 &=\epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\\
 &=\frac1{726}+\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}\epsilon^{2/3}
 +o(\epsilon^{2/3}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) is regular for both designs, both bridge contrasts equal \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty.
\]
On the relatively open subregion \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\subseteq\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\), every design remains regular and identifies \(\tau\), \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\), \(D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)=\infty.
\]
For each prescribed \(\chi>1\), the center cost vector belongs to \(\mathcal C_\kappa\), has paired-cost ratio exactly \(\chi\), and has a relatively open neighborhood in \(\mathcal C_\kappa\) on which \(d_{\mathrm p}\) remains strictly more expensive and uniquely diagnostic-selected for all sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\), while both the arm-normalized and balanced-center IKM-normalized ratios diverge along the center-law path. Thus selection by this paper's paired-source residual-risk diagnostic has no finite uniform efficiency guarantee even when its chosen design is required to bear any prescribed finite cost disadvantage; even the least-divergent cost-disadvantage sequence grows at order \(\epsilon^{-2/3}\), and its ratio retains the leading divergence \(1/(726\epsilon^2)\). This result concerns only the newly defined diagnostic. It neither attributes a proxy-selection rule to a published paper nor refutes predictive proxy selection generally. The IKM-normalized profile has its absolute causal-efficiency interpretation only under the separately stated fixed-system premises; the arm-normalized profile is a source-score design value on the full regular class and a gradient design value only on bridge-differentiable submodels.

defs.def:binary-witness:
Fix an arbitrary prescribed \(\chi>1\). Set \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=(5\chi-3)/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=(5\chi-3)/2\), and put
\[
 y_{\chi}=\sqrt{1-\frac{3}{10\chi}}.
\]
Let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form
\[
 Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}),
\]
while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{y_{\chi}}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then
\[
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi-1}{2},\qquad
 c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi+1}{2},\qquad
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2,\qquad c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3,
\]
so the paired costs are \(5\chi\) and \(5\), respectively. For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are
\[
 h_d(l,a)=\frac{l}{y},
 \qquad
 q_d(e,a)=\frac{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)}{1-1/16},
\]
and the residual prediction variance is
\[
 R(x,y)=\frac{(1-x^2)(1-y^2)}{1-x^2y^2}.
\]

The \emph{binary constrained finite-cell model} \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\) is the family of laws \(P\) with the preceding prescribed catalogue, costs, cap, and role assignments, constant \(X\) and constant \(S_{2d}\), latent variables \(U,T,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4\in\{-1,1\}\), \(A=(T+1)/2\), and potential variables
\[
 Z(a)=(W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4),\qquad Y(a)=U,
 \qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For strictly positive probability vectors \((\pi_g:g\in\{E,O\})\), \((\nu_u:u\in\{-1,1\})\), \((\lambda_t:t\in\{-1,1\})\), observational treatment kernels \(e_u(t)\), and proxy kernels \(k_{j,u}(w)\), its latent-cell mass factorizes as
\[
 P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
 =\pi_g\nu_u\bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t
 +\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}
 \prod_{j=1}^4k_{j,u}(w_j). \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(U\) is independent of \(G\), treatment is randomized independently of \(U\) in source \(E\), and the four proxies are mutually independent conditional on \(U\) and invariant across source and treatment. The design \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \((W_1,W_2)\) to roles one and three, and \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \((W_3,W_4)\) to roles one and three; role two is constant. For each \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), the preceding center \(P_\epsilon\) is the point having \(\pi_E=\pi_O=1/2\), \(\nu_{-1}=\nu_1=1/2\), \(\lambda_{-1}=\lambda_1=1/2\), \(e_u(t)=(1+tu/4)/2\), and
\[
 k_{j,u}(w)=\frac{1+s_juw}{2},
 \qquad
 (s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4)=(\epsilon,y_{\chi},1/2,1/2).
\]
The model is parameterized by the relative interiors of these finite probability simplices. Its relative topology is equivalently the Euclidean parameter topology or the maximum-norm topology \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{cell}}\) induced by the complete latent-cell vector in (1).
defs.def:regular-law-class: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) is the subclass of \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) satisfying long- and short-term consistency, observational latent exchangeability and overlap, experimental randomization and overlap, full short-term external validity, source support, the sequential-outcome restriction, and both proxy-completeness conditions for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
defs.def:predictive-benchmark:
For each \(d\in\mathcal D\), compute the observational residual prediction risk
\[
R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O]
\]
and define the newly introduced paired-source diagnostic
\[
\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=\frac{(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)}{B}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\) retain every minimizer of this diagnostic, and define
\[
\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=
\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
{\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
The notation records that the diagnostic is shaped by a residual-risk-per-budget calculation; it is not attributed as a proxy-selection workflow or guarantee of Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile:
For \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and \(0<\alpha<1\), set
\[
\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=\frac{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}{\alpha}+\frac{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}{1-\alpha}.
\]
Set the value to \(+\infty\) outside the observable regular set.
defs.def:common-identification-class:
\[
\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}
=\{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}:\theta_d(P)=\tau\text{ for every }d\in\mathcal D\}.
\]
defs.def:ikmw-normalized-design-value:
For each regular design \(d\), define the source scores on the Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang normalization by
\[
 \psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{E,1})\phi_{E,d},
 \qquad
 \psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{O,1})\phi_{O,d},
\]
and define their source-conditional second moments by
\[
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=E]
 =(1-p_{E,1})^2V_{E,d},
\]
\[
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=O]
 =(1-p_{O,1})^2V_{O,d}.
\]
The profiled IKM-normalized value, its optimizer set, and the best-tie paired-source diagnostic approximation ratio are
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
 =\left(
 \sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 +\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \right)^2,
\]
\[
 D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
 =\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d',\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}.
\]
These objects are defined only as normalization-specific score moments and profiles. Their interpretation as causal efficiency bounds is supplied design by design by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\) after its causal-identification and regularity premises have been verified.

assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-outcomes: \((Y(a),S_{3d}(a))\perp S_{1d}(a)\mid S_{2d}(a),U,X,G=O\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:late-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{3d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:early-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{1d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:observed-outcome-bridge-existence:
For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(h_d\) is a square-integrable solution of
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O]
=\mathbb E_P[h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O].
\]
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile:
For \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and \(0<\alpha<1\), set
\[
\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=\frac{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}{\alpha}+\frac{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}{1-\alpha}.
\]
Set the value to \(+\infty\) outside the observable regular set.

assumptions.ass:observed-outcome-bridge-existence:
For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(h_d\) is a square-integrable solution of
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O]
=\mathbb E_P[h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O].
\]
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(\chi>1\) and \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), and write \(P_{\chi,\epsilon}=P_\epsilon\) for the binary center in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\), with the dependence on \(\chi\) made explicit. Then \(P_{\chi,\epsilon}\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), both designwise bridge contrasts equal \(\tau=0\), and
\[
 R_{d_{\mathrm p}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\frac{3}{10\chi}\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2(1-3/(10\chi))}
 <\frac{3}{10\chi}<\frac3{10}<\frac35
 =R_{d_{\mathrm e}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon}).
\]
Consequently \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\) and \(D^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\). The raw-risk-selected design is costlier in each source:
\[
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}-c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}
 =c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}-c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}
 =\frac{5(\chi-1)}2>0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 V_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{40\chi}{10\chi-3},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}\left(\epsilon^{-2}+14\right),
 \qquad
 \mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e}}^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=\frac{3872}{25},
\]
and the exact center ratio is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 &=\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\\
 &=\frac{25}{3872}
 \left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{20\chi(5\chi-1)}{10\chi-3}}
 +\sqrt{\frac{32(5\chi+1)}{75(10\chi-3)}
 \left(\epsilon^{-2}+14\right)}
 \right\}^{2}.                                             \tag{1}
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 \ge
 \frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}
 \left(\epsilon^{-2}+14\right)
 >\frac{\epsilon^{-2}+14}{726},                            \tag{2}
\]
with the identical inequalities for \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\), and
\[
 \inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 >\frac{\epsilon^{-2}+14}{726}.                            \tag{3}
\]
For all sufficiently small \(\epsilon\), the infimum in (3) is attained. If \(\chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)\) is any minimizer and
\[
 k_\star=\frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15},
\]
then
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)
 \sim k_\star\epsilon^{-2/3}.                              \tag{4}
\]
Equivalently, on writing \(\chi=k\epsilon^{-2/3}\), the coefficient of \(\epsilon^{2/3}\) inside the braces-squared expression before multiplication by \(25/3872\) is
\[
 q(k)=2\sqrt{\frac{32k}{15}}+\frac{8}{75k},                \tag{5}
\]
and \(q\) has the unique minimizer \(k_\star\). The sharp second-order uniform elbow is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 &=\epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\\
 &=\frac1{726}+\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}\epsilon^{2/3}
 +o(\epsilon^{2/3}).                                      \tag{6}
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular, the first-order limit in (6) is \(1/726\).

defs.def:binary-witness:
Fix an arbitrary prescribed \(\chi>1\). Set \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=(5\chi-3)/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=(5\chi-3)/2\), and put
\[
 y_{\chi}=\sqrt{1-\frac{3}{10\chi}}.
\]
Let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form
\[
 Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}),
\]
while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{y_{\chi}}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then
\[
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi-1}{2},\qquad
 c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi+1}{2},\qquad
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2,\qquad c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3,
\]
so the paired costs are \(5\chi\) and \(5\), respectively. For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are
\[
 h_d(l,a)=\frac{l}{y},
 \qquad
 q_d(e,a)=\frac{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)}{1-1/16},
\]
and the residual prediction variance is
\[
 R(x,y)=\frac{(1-x^2)(1-y^2)}{1-x^2y^2}.
\]
The primary prediction selector compares this unweighted residual risk itself; paired-cost weighting is retained only as a secondary diagnostic.

The \emph{binary constrained finite-cell model} \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\) is the family of laws \(P\) with the preceding prescribed catalogue, costs, cap, and role assignments, constant \(X\) and constant \(S_{2d}\), latent variables \(U,T,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4\in\{-1,1\}\), \(A=(T+1)/2\), and potential variables
\[
 Z(a)=(W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4),\qquad Y(a)=U,
 \qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For strictly positive probability vectors \((\pi_g:g\in\{E,O\})\), \((\nu_u:u\in\{-1,1\})\), \((\lambda_t:t\in\{-1,1\})\), observational treatment kernels \(e_u(t)\), and proxy kernels \(k_{j,u}(w)\), its latent-cell mass factorizes as
\[
 P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
 =\pi_g\nu_u\bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t
 +\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}
 \prod_{j=1}^4k_{j,u}(w_j). \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(U\) is independent of \(G\), treatment is randomized independently of \(U\) in source \(E\), and the four proxies are mutually independent conditional on \(U\) and invariant across source and treatment. The design \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \((W_1,W_2)\) to roles one and three, and \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \((W_3,W_4)\) to roles one and three; role two is constant. For each \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), the preceding center \(P_\epsilon\) is the point having \(\pi_E=\pi_O=1/2\), \(\nu_{-1}=\nu_1=1/2\), \(\lambda_{-1}=\lambda_1=1/2\), \(e_u(t)=(1+tu/4)/2\), and
\[
 k_{j,u}(w)=\frac{1+s_juw}{2},
 \qquad
 (s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4)=(\epsilon,y_{\chi},1/2,1/2).
\]
The model is parameterized by the relative interiors of these finite probability simplices. Its relative topology is equivalently the Euclidean parameter topology or the maximum-norm topology \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{cell}}\) induced by the complete latent-cell vector in (1).
defs.def:regular-law-class: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) is the subclass of \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) satisfying long- and short-term consistency, observational latent exchangeability and overlap, experimental randomization and overlap, full short-term external validity, source support, the sequential-outcome restriction, and both proxy-completeness conditions for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
defs.def:predictive-benchmark:
For each \(d\in\mathcal D\), compute the observational residual prediction risk
\[
R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O].
\]
The generic raw population prediction-risk rule retains every tie:
\[
\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}R_d(P).
\]
Its best-tie profiled design-value ratio is
\[
\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=
\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
{\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
For comparison only, define the continuous paired-source count and the secondary cost-weighted residual-risk diagnostic
\[
n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=\frac{B}{c_{E,d}+c_{O,d}},
\qquad
\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)
=\frac{R_d(P)}{n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)}
=\frac{(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)}{B}.
\]
This secondary quantity does not define \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\) or \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\). The subscript records only the residual-risk-per-budget shape and does not attribute a proxy-selection workflow or guarantee to Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile:
For \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and \(0<\alpha<1\), set
\[
\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=\frac{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}{\alpha}+\frac{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}{1-\alpha}.
\]
Set the value to \(+\infty\) outside the observable regular set.
defs.def:common-identification-class:
\[
\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}
=\{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}:\theta_d(P)=\tau\text{ for every }d\in\mathcal D\}.
\]
defs.def:ikmw-normalized-design-value:
For each regular design \(d\), define the source scores on the Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang normalization by
\[
 \psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{E,1})\phi_{E,d},
 \qquad
 \psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=(1-p_{O,1})\phi_{O,d},
\]
and define their source-conditional second moments by
\[
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=E]
 =(1-p_{E,1})^2V_{E,d},
\]
\[
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P[(\psi_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}})^2\mid G=O]
 =(1-p_{O,1})^2V_{O,d}.
\]
The profiled IKM-normalized value, its optimizer set, and the best-tie raw population prediction-risk ratio are
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
 =\left(
 \sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 +\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \right)^2,
\]
\[
 D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)
 =\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P),
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d',\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}.
\]
These objects are defined only as normalization-specific score moments and profiles. Their interpretation as causal efficiency bounds is supplied design by design by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\) after its causal-identification and regularity premises have been verified.

assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-outcomes: \((Y(a),S_{3d}(a))\perp S_{1d}(a)\mid S_{2d}(a),U,X,G=O\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:late-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{3d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:early-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{1d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:observed-outcome-bridge-existence:
For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(h_d\) is a square-integrable solution of
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O]
=\mathbb E_P[h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O].
\]
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and abbreviate
\[
 p_d=R_d(P),
 \qquad v_d=\mathcal V_d^*(P).
\]
Define the raw-prediction-order relation and its order-restricted design-value constant by
\[
 \mathcal O_P=\{(d,d')\in\mathcal D^2:p_d\le p_{d'}\},
 \qquad
 C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)=\max_{(d,d')\in\mathcal O_P}\frac{v_d}{v_{d'}}. \tag{1}
\]
Then \(1\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty\), and, for every \(C\ge0\),
\[
 \bigl[p_d\le p_{d'}\Longrightarrow v_d\le C v_{d'}
 \text{ for all }d,d'\in\mathcal D\bigr]
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C\ge C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P). \tag{2}
\]
The smallest constant for the actual best-tie raw prediction-risk rule is
\[
 C_{\mathrm{sel}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}v_d}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}v_{d'}}
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P),
 \qquad
 1\le C_{\mathrm{sel}}(P)\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty. \tag{3}
\]
Consequently, for any nonempty subclass \(\mathcal Q\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), a finite constant uniform over \(\mathcal Q\) exists for the best-tie rule if and only if \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)<\infty\); for all pairwise raw-risk-order implications it exists if and only if \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty\). Thus (1), rather than an operator norm, is the weakest exact lawwise comparison for selection by raw population prediction risk. The design-specific operators \(T_d\) enter (1) through the bridges and hence through \(v_d\), but no further comparison of the operators is necessary for lawwise finiteness.

More specifically, consider any numerical realization of the handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{comp}}\) with the following properties. For each \(d\), it supplies a real vector space \(\mathcal H_d\), a cone \(\mathcal X_d(P)\subseteq\mathcal H_d\setminus\{0\}\) containing a transported law-specific direction \(x_d(P)\), a positive prediction quadratic form \(Q_{R,d}\) on that cone, and two nonnegative source-score quadratic forms \(Q_{E,d}\) and \(Q_{O,d}\), with
\[
 p_d=Q_{R,d}\{x_d(P)\},
 \qquad v_d=F_d\{x_d(P)\}, \tag{4}
\]
where
\[
 F_d(x)=\left\{\sqrt{c_{E,d}Q_{E,d}(x)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}Q_{O,d}(x)}\right\}^2. \tag{5}
\]
On the bridge-differentiable submodel class of Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}bridge\text{-}differentiable\text{-}submodel}\), these source scores are gradient components; outside that class, only the source-score interpretation is asserted. Set
\[
 \Lambda_-(P)=\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\inf_{x\in\mathcal X_d(P)}\frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}(x)},
 \qquad
 \Lambda_+(P)=\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X_d(P)}\frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}(x)}. \tag{6}
\]
The weakest two-sided quadratic-form envelope on the chosen cones is precisely
\[
 0<\Lambda_-(P)\le\Lambda_+(P)<\infty, \tag{7}
\]
and it implies the valid, generally conservative certificate
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)\le\frac{\Lambda_+(P)}{\Lambda_-(P)}. \tag{8}
\]

The sharp constant in (2) or (3) is not, in general, a largest generalized eigenvalue. Indeed,
\[
 F_d(x)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\left\{
 \frac{c_{E,d}Q_{E,d}(x)}{\alpha}
 +\frac{c_{O,d}Q_{O,d}(x)}{1-\alpha}\right\}, \tag{9}
\]
so the profiled numerator is generally not a quadratic form. If \(\mathcal H_d\) is finite dimensional, \(Q_{R,d}\) is positive definite, and \(\mathcal X_d(P)=\mathcal H_d\setminus\{0\}\), a largest generalized eigenvalue at a fixed \(\alpha\) gives only a one-sided full-space envelope. Selection requires both the upper and lower envelopes in (6), and equality in (8) additionally requires saturation by law-realized, raw-risk-ordered directions. Hence equality with a largest generalized eigenvalue can hold only after adding a common-space representation, a normalization of the positive lower envelope, and the required saturation; none follows from observable-law operator bijectivity or from the raw-risk ordering alone.

defs.def:bridge-differentiable-submodel:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(d\in\mathcal D\), and write
\[
 H_d=(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X),\qquad L_d=(S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X).
\]
A regular two-source parametric submodel \(\{P_t:|t|<t_0\}\) through \(P=P_0\), with source-conditional scores \(\ell_E\) and \(\ell_O\), is called \emph{bridge-differentiable for design \(d\) at \(P\)} when the following conditions hold.  First, the source-conditional laws are dominated on a common support and the path is differentiable in quadratic mean in each source.  Second, for all sufficiently small \(|t|\), \(P_t\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and its design-\(d\) outcome bridge \(h_{d,t}\) is unique.  Third, after identifying the common \(L_2\) coordinate spaces along the dominated path, there is \(\dot h_d\in L_2(H_d\mid G=O)\) such that
\[
 \left\|\frac{h_{d,t}-h_{d,0}}{t}-\dot h_d\right\|_{L_2(P(\cdot\mid G=O))}\longrightarrow0,
\]
and the conditional bridge equation
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_t}\{Y-h_{d,t}(H_d)\mid L_d,G=O\}=0
\]
may be differentiated at \(t=0\) in \(L_2(L_d\mid G=O)\) using the conditional-score rule.  This is a restriction on submodels, not a consequence of pointwise bijectivity of \(T_d\).
defs.def:operator-comparison-handle: Use \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{comp}}\) to compare the source-score quadratic forms underlying \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)\) with the raw residual-risk quadratic form underlying \(R_d(P)\). These source-score forms have a gradient interpretation only along the bridge-differentiable paths declared for design \(d\). The exact target is a lawwise constant bounding the raw-risk selector ratio \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\); the handle does not assert that a generalized eigenvalue is sharp and does not give an unconditional gradient or causal-efficiency interpretation.

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), the exact fixed-catalogue raw-risk-selection identity is
\[
 1\le\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}
 (\sqrt{c_{E,d'}V_{E,d'}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d'}V_{O,d'}})^2}<\infty.
\]
The smallest constant in the actual best-tie inequality is exactly \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\). The least constant that makes every pairwise implication
\(R_d(P)\le R_{d'}(P)\Rightarrow \mathcal V_d^*(P)\le C(P)\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\)
valid is
\[
 \max_{\substack{d,d'\in\mathcal D:\,R_d(P)\le R_{d'}(P)}}
 \frac{\mathcal V_d^*(P)}{\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
Every displayed constant is finite at a fixed \(P\). Nevertheless, for every prescribed finite \(\chi>1\), the \(\chi\)-indexed binary region satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\infty\), even though the uniquely raw-risk-selected design has paired cost \(\chi\) times that of the arm-normalized source-score-optimal design at the center laws. Across all center cost-disadvantage factors, every minimizing sequence satisfies
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)
 \sim\frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15}\epsilon^{-2/3},
\]
and the exact least-divergent envelope obeys
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 &=\epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\\
 &=\frac1{726}+\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}\epsilon^{2/3}
 +o(\epsilon^{2/3}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) yields an exact law-specific enumeration, not a primitive uniform raw-risk-to-source-score guarantee; optimizing the witness's cost disadvantage does not remove the leading \(1/(726\epsilon^2)\) divergence.

defs.def:predictive-benchmark:
For each \(d\in\mathcal D\), compute the observational residual prediction risk
\[
R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}\mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O].
\]
The generic raw population prediction-risk rule retains every tie:
\[
\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}R_d(P).
\]
Its best-tie profiled design-value ratio is
\[
\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=
\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
{\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.
\]
For comparison only, define the continuous paired-source count and the secondary cost-weighted residual-risk diagnostic
\[
n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=\frac{B}{c_{E,d}+c_{O,d}},
\qquad
\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)
=\frac{R_d(P)}{n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)}
=\frac{(c_{E,d}+c_{O,d})R_d(P)}{B}.
\]
This secondary quantity does not define \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\) or \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\). The subscript records only the residual-risk-per-budget shape and does not attribute a proxy-selection workflow or guarantee to Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile:
For \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and \(0<\alpha<1\), set
\[
\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=\frac{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}{\alpha}+\frac{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}{1-\alpha}.
\]
Set the value to \(+\infty\) outside the observable regular set.

assumptions.ass:observed-outcome-bridge-existence:
For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(h_d\) is a square-integrable solution of
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O]
=\mathbb E_P[h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O].
\]
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

snapshot.stmt:
Fix any prescribed \(\chi>1\) and use Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}witness}\). For every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), \(P_\epsilon\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\), both admissible bridge contrasts equal \(\tau=0\), the unique raw population prediction-risk optimizer is \(d_{\mathrm p}\), and the unique arm-normalized design-value optimizer is \(d_{\mathrm e}\). More precisely,
\[
 R_{d_{\mathrm p}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac{3}{10\chi}\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2(1-3/(10\chi))}
 <\frac{3}{10\chi}<\frac3{10}<\frac35
 =R_{d_{\mathrm e}}(P_\epsilon).
\]
The paired costs and the secondary cost-weighted prediction objectives satisfy
\[
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=5\chi,
 \qquad
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}+c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=5,
\]
\[
 B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}(P_\epsilon;B)
 =\frac32\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2y_\chi^2}
 <\frac32<3
 =B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm e}}(P_\epsilon;B).
\]
Moreover,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}
 +\frac{896}{75(10\chi-3)},
 \qquad
 \mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e}}^*(P_\epsilon)=\frac{3872}{25},
\]
and, as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) with \(\chi\) fixed,
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)
 =\frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}
 +O_\chi(\epsilon^{-1}).
\]
For each fixed pair \((\chi,\epsilon)\), there is a radius \(r_\epsilon>0\) such that every law \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\) with \(\|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<r_\epsilon\) is regular, has the same strict raw-risk and arm-normalized optimizer assignments, has both bridge contrasts equal to \(\tau\), and satisfies \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)>\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P_\epsilon)/2\).

defs.def:binary-witness:
Fix an arbitrary prescribed \(\chi>1\). Set \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=(5\chi-3)/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=(5\chi-3)/2\), and put
\[
 y_{\chi}=\sqrt{1-\frac{3}{10\chi}}.
\]
Let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form
\[
 Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}),
\]
while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{y_{\chi}}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then
\[
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi-1}{2},\qquad
 c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi+1}{2},\qquad
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2,\qquad c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3,
\]
so the paired costs are \(5\chi\) and \(5\), respectively. For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are
\[
 h_d(l,a)=\frac{l}{y},
 \qquad
 q_d(e,a)=\frac{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)}{1-1/16},
\]
and the residual prediction variance is
\[
 R(x,y)=\frac{(1-x^2)(1-y^2)}{1-x^2y^2}.
\]
The primary prediction selector compares this unweighted residual risk itself; paired-cost weighting is retained only as a secondary diagnostic.

The \emph{binary constrained finite-cell model} \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\) is the family of laws \(P\) with the preceding prescribed catalogue, costs, cap, and role assignments, constant \(X\) and constant \(S_{2d}\), latent variables \(U,T,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4\in\{-1,1\}\), \(A=(T+1)/2\), and potential variables
\[
 Z(a)=(W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4),\qquad Y(a)=U,
 \qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For strictly positive probability vectors \((\pi_g:g\in\{E,O\})\), \((\nu_u:u\in\{-1,1\})\), \((\lambda_t:t\in\{-1,1\})\), observational treatment kernels \(e_u(t)\), and proxy kernels \(k_{j,u}(w)\), its latent-cell mass factorizes as
\[
 P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
 =\pi_g\nu_u\bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t
 +\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}
 \prod_{j=1}^4k_{j,u}(w_j). \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(U\) is independent of \(G\), treatment is randomized independently of \(U\) in source \(E\), and the four proxies are mutually independent conditional on \(U\) and invariant across source and treatment. The design \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \((W_1,W_2)\) to roles one and three, and \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \((W_3,W_4)\) to roles one and three; role two is constant. For each \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), the preceding center \(P_\epsilon\) is the point having \(\pi_E=\pi_O=1/2\), \(\nu_{-1}=\nu_1=1/2\), \(\lambda_{-1}=\lambda_1=1/2\), \(e_u(t)=(1+tu/4)/2\), and
\[
 k_{j,u}(w)=\frac{1+s_juw}{2},
 \qquad
 (s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4)=(\epsilon,y_{\chi},1/2,1/2).
\]
The model is parameterized by the relative interiors of these finite probability simplices. Its relative topology is equivalently the Euclidean parameter topology or the maximum-norm topology \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{cell}}\) induced by the complete latent-cell vector in (1).
